sentences.zh: 唐制有內侍省，其官員：內侍四人；

translations.literal: Under the Tang system there was the Palace Domestic Service; its officials were: four Palace Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang institutional code provided for a Palace Domestic Service with these officers: four Palace Attendants;

sentences.zh: 內常侍六人；

translations.literal: six Inner Regular Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: six Inner Regular Attendants;

sentences.zh: 內謁者監六人；

translations.literal: six Supervisors of Inner Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: six Supervisors of Inner Palace Messengers;

sentences.zh: 內給事八人；

translations.literal: eight Inner Grooms of the Chamber;
translations.idiomatic: eight Inner Chamberlains;

sentences.zh: 謁者十二人；

translations.literal: twelve Messengers;
translations.idiomatic: twelve Messengers-at-Court;

sentences.zh: 典引十八人；

translations.literal: eighteen Directors of Introduction;
translations.idiomatic: eighteen Directors of Introduction;

sentences.zh: 寺伯二人；

translations.literal: two Palace Stewards;
translations.idiomatic: two Palace Stewards;

sentences.zh: 寺人六人。

translations.literal: six Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: six Palace Servants.

sentences.zh: 別有五局：掖廷局掌宮人簿籍；

translations.literal: In addition there were five bureaus: the Rear Palace Bureau managed the registers of palace women;
translations.idiomatic: There were also five bureaus apart from these: the Rear Palace Bureau kept the roster books of palace women;

sentences.zh: 宮闈局掌宮內門禁，其屬有掌扇、給使等員；

translations.literal: the Inner Gate Bureau managed inner-palace gate security; under it were such posts as fan-bearers and supply attendants;
translations.idiomatic: the Inner Gate Bureau controlled access within the palace gates, with subordinates including fan-bearers and supply attendants;

sentences.zh: 奚官局掌宮人疾病死喪；

translations.literal: the Wardrobe Bureau managed illness, death, and funerals of palace women;
translations.idiomatic: the Wardrobe and Commissary Bureau oversaw the sickness, death, and burial of palace women;

sentences.zh: 內僕局掌宮中供帳燈燭；

translations.literal: the Inner Servants Bureau managed palace provisioning of bedding, lamps, and candles;
translations.idiomatic: the Inner Servants Bureau was in charge of bedding, lighting, and candles within the palace;

sentences.zh: 內府局主中藏給納。

translations.literal: the Inner Treasury Bureau presided over the central storehouses for distribution and receipt.
translations.idiomatic: the Inner Treasury Bureau administered the central stores and their issue and intake.

sentences.zh: 五局有令丞，皆內官為之。

translations.literal: The five bureaus had directors and assistant directors, all filled by inner officials.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the five bureaus had a chief and deputies, and all were filled by eunuch officials.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，太宗定制，內侍省不置三品官，內侍是長官，階四品。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, Taizong fixed regulations: the Palace Domestic Service did not appoint third-rank officials; the Palace Attendant was the chief, at fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan, Emperor Taizong laid down rules whereby the Palace Domestic Service had no third-rank posts; the Palace Attendant served as its head at the fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 至永淳末，向七十年，權未假於內官，但在閣門守禦，黃衣廩食而已。

translations.literal: By the end of Yongchun, for nearly seventy years, power was not lent to inner officials; they only guarded and defended at the gate pavilions, yellow-robed with grain rations, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the close of the Yongchun era—nearly seventy years—inner officials had not been granted authority; they merely stood guard at the gatehouses in yellow robes on palace rations, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 則天稱制，二十年間，差增員位。

translations.literal: When Wu Zetian assumed the regency, over twenty years the posts were gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu held the reins of government, over two decades she steadily increased the establishment.

sentences.zh: 中宗性慈，務崇恩貸，神龍中，宦官三千餘人，超授七品以上員外官者千餘人，然衣硃紫者尚寡。

translations.literal: Zhongzong was by nature compassionate and devoted himself to generous grace; in the Shenlong era there were more than three thousand eunuchs, and over a thousand were given supernumerary offices of seventh rank or above, yet those wearing vermillion and purple were still few.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong was mild by nature and lavished favors; during Shenlong more than three thousand eunuchs served at court, and over a thousand received supernumerary appointments of seventh rank or higher—yet few yet wore the vermilion and purple of high office.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在位既久，崇重宮禁，中官稍稱旨者，即授三品、左右監門將軍，得門施棨戟。

translations.literal: After Xuanzong had reigned long, he honored and stressed the palace precincts; inner officials who somewhat pleased him were immediately given third rank and the post of Left or Right Gate Guardian General, and could display halberds at their gates.
translations.idiomatic: As Xuanzong's reign lengthened, he exalted the inner palace; any eunuch who pleased him even slightly might be made a third-rank minister and appointed Left or Right Gate Guardian General, with ceremonial halberds set before his gate.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶中，長安大內、大明、興慶三宮，皇子十宅院，皇孫百孫院。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, in Chang'an the Great Inner Palace, Daming, and Xingqing palaces, the Ten Princely Residences for imperial sons, and the Hundred-Grandsons Court for imperial grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan and Tianbao, Chang'an boasted the Great Inner, Daming, and Xingqing palaces, the ten princely mansions, and the Hundred Grandsons compounds.

sentences.zh: 東都大內、上陽兩宮，大率宮女四萬人，品官黃衣已上三千人，衣硃紫者千餘人。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Capital the Great Inner and Shangyang palaces; altogether palace women numbered about forty thousand, ranked officials in yellow robes and above about three thousand, those in vermillion and purple over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern capital stood the Great Inner and Shangyang palaces; altogether there were roughly forty thousand palace women, some three thousand eunuch officials of yellow rank and above, and more than a thousand in vermilion and purple.

sentences.zh: 後李輔國從幸靈武，程元振翼衛代宗，怙寵邀君，乃至守三公，封王爵，干預國政，亦未全握兵權。

translations.literal: Later Li Fuguo followed the emperor to Lingwu, Cheng Yuanzhen escorted and guarded Daizong; relying on favor they curried the ruler, so that they reached holding the Three Excellencies, were enfeoffed as princes, and intervened in state affairs—yet they still did not fully grasp military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Fuguo accompanied the court to Lingwu and Cheng Yuanzhen guarded the heir who became Daizong; flaunting imperial favor they lorded over the throne, rose to the Three Excellencies and princely titles, and meddled in government—yet even they did not wholly monopolize military power.

sentences.zh: 代宗時，子儀北伐，親王東討，遂特立觀軍容宣慰使，命魚朝恩為之，然自有統帥，亦監領而已。

translations.literal: In the time of Daizong, when Ziyi campaigned north and imperial princes campaigned east, they specially established the post of Army Supervision Commissioner and Pacification Envoy, appointing Yu Chao'en to it; yet there were still commanders in their own right—it was merely supervisory.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daizong, with Guo Ziyi campaigning north and imperial princes campaigning east, the court created the post of Army Supervision and Pacification Commissioner and gave it to Yu Chao'en—but each army still had its own commander; his role was oversight alone.

sentences.zh: 德宗避涇師之難，幸山南，內官竇文場、霍仙鳴擁從。

translations.literal: Dezong escaped the crisis of the Jingzhou mutiny and went to Shannan; the inner officials Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming attended and escorted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong fled the mutiny of the Jing army and took refuge in Shannan, the eunuchs Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming went with him.

sentences.zh: 賊平之後，不欲武臣典重兵，其左右神策、天威等軍，欲委宦者主之。

translations.literal: After the rebels were pacified, he did not wish military men to hold heavy armies; the Left and Right Shence and Tianwei armies, he wished to entrust to eunuchs to command.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he was unwilling to leave powerful armies in the hands of generals, and intended to place the Left and Right Shence and Tianwei guards under eunuch command.

sentences.zh: 乃置護軍中尉兩員、中護軍兩員，分掌禁兵，以文場、仙鳴為兩中尉，自是神策親軍之權，全歸於宦者矣。

translations.literal: He then established two Protector Army Central Commanders and two Central Army Protectors to divide command of the forbidden troops; Wenchang and Xianming were made the two Central Commanders—from this the authority of the Shence personal army wholly passed to eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore created two Central Commanders of the Army Protectorate and two Deputy Protectors to split control of the palace guards, naming Wenchang and Xianming the two Central Commanders; from that point the Shence personal army belonged entirely to the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 自貞元之後，威權日熾，蘭锜將臣，率皆子蓄；

translations.literal: From after Zhenyuan their power and authority grew daily; for orchid-awning generals and ministers, most were kept as adopted sons;
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhenyuan era their power swelled day by day; leading generals and ministers were mostly enrolled as their adoptive sons;

sentences.zh: 籓方戎帥，必以賄成；

translations.literal: frontier military governors invariably secured their posts through bribes;
translations.idiomatic: regional commanders invariably bought their appointments with bribes;

sentences.zh: 萬機之與奪任情，九重之廢立由己。

translations.literal: bestowal and seizure of the myriad affairs of state at their whim; deposition and installation within the Ninefold Enclosure by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: they disposed of state business as they pleased, and made or unmade emperors within the forbidden palace.

sentences.zh: 元和之季，毒被乘輿。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe, poison reached the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Yuanhe era poison touched the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 長慶纘隆，徒郁枕幹之憤；

translations.literal: Changqing succeeded to the throne, but only nurtured resentment over the pillow and trunk;
translations.idiomatic: When Changqing ascended the throne, he brooded in vain over wrongs done at the pillow and at Gan;

sentences.zh: 臨軒暇逸，旋忘塗地之冤。

translations.literal: at the imperial audience he sought leisure and ease, and soon forgot the injustice of those who lay smeared on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: enthroned, he soon gave himself to ease and forgot the blood shed at his feet.

sentences.zh: 而易月未除，滔天盡怒。

translations.literal: Yet before the mourning month was ended, heaven-filling wrath was unleashed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet before the mourning period had passed, wrath flooded heaven.

sentences.zh: 甲第名園之賜，莫匪伶官；

translations.literal: grants of mansions and famous gardens were none but to actor-officials;
translations.idiomatic: The gift of great houses and renowned gardens went only to actor-favorites of the eunuchs;

sentences.zh: 硃袍紫綬之榮，無非巷伯。

translations.literal: the glory of vermillion robes and purple cords was none but to alley stewards.
translations.idiomatic: vermilion robes and purple sashes adorned none but eunuch gatekeepers.

sentences.zh: 是時高品白身之數，四千六百一十八人，內則參秉戎權，外則臨監籓嶽。

translations.literal: At that time those of high rank or commoner status numbered 4,618; within they shared military authority, without they supervised the frontier commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time they numbered 4,618, from high rank down to plain attendants—within they shared military power, without they oversaw the provinces.

sentences.zh: 文宗包祖宗之恥，痛肘腋之仇，思翦厲階，去其太甚。

translations.literal: Wenzong embraced the shame of the ancestors and grieved the enemy at his armpit; he thought to cut down the growing stalk and remove the excess.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong nursed the humiliation left by his forebears and smarted at the enemy beside his throne; he sought to cut the evil at its root and curb the worst excesses.

sentences.zh: 宋申錫言未出口，尋以破家；

translations.literal: Song Shenxi's words had not left his mouth before his household was ruined;
translations.idiomatic: Song Shenxi had scarcely spoken before his family was destroyed;

sentences.zh: 李仲言謀之不臧，幾乎敗國。

translations.literal: Li Zhongyan's plotting was ill-conceived and nearly ruined the state;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongyan's conspiracy went awry and nearly wrecked the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 何、竇之徒轉蹙，讓、珪之勢尤狂，五十餘年，禍胎逾煽，昭宗之季，所不忍聞。

translations.literal: He, Dou, and their kind pressed tighter; Rang and Gui's power was yet more frenzied; for fifty-odd years the womb of disaster burned ever hotter—at the end of Zhaozong, what one cannot bear to hear.
translations.idiomatic: The factions of He and Dou tightened their grip; Rang and Gui grew wilder still; for more than fifty years the seeds of ruin only blazed brighter—by Emperor Zhaozong's day the tale becomes unbearable.

sentences.zh: 臣遍覽前書，考茲覆轍，試言大較，庶竭其源。

translations.literal: Your servant has read through the earlier histories and examined these overturned tracks; I venture to speak in broad outline, hoping to exhaust the source.
translations.idiomatic: Having surveyed the earlier histories and traced these repeated calamities, I shall sketch the main pattern in hope of laying bare the root cause.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 自書契已來，不無閽寺，況垂之天象，備見職官。

translations.literal: Since written contracts there have never been without gate and temple officials; moreover it is handed down in the celestial signs and fully appears among official posts.
translations.idiomatic: Since the age of writing there have always been palace gatekeepers and eunuchs; the heavens themselves reflect their station, and the bureaucratic tables provide for them.

sentences.zh: 即如秦皇、漢武，宮闈之內，宦官以侍宴遊。

translations.literal: Take Qin Huangdi and Han Wudi: within the palace women, eunuchs served at banquets and excursions.
translations.idiomatic: Even Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi employed eunuchs within the inner quarters to attend banquets and outings.

sentences.zh: 但英睿之君，措置斯得；

translations.literal: but enlightened and perceptive rulers placed them appropriately;
translations.idiomatic: Yet sagacious rulers knew how to place them properly;

sentences.zh: 及荒僻之主，奢蕩是求。

translations.literal: when dissolute lords who strayed to wilderness came, luxury and dissipation were what they sought.
translations.idiomatic: whereas debauched sovereigns sought only indulgence.

sentences.zh: 委番、棸、蹶、楀之徒，飾姬姜狗馬之玩，外言不入，惟欲是從。

translations.literal: They entrusted Fan, Zong, Jue, Yu and such, adorned with the diversions of beauties and dog-and-horse pleasures; outside words did not enter—they followed only desire.
translations.idiomatic: They entrusted themselves to favorites such as Zhao Gao and Zhang Rang, dallying with women and hounds; no counsel from outside could reach them—they followed desire alone.

sentences.zh: 雖並列五侯，猶為賞薄；

translations.literal: though all five marquises were ranked together, it was still regarded as thin reward;
translations.idiomatic: Even enfeoffing the Five Marquises at once seemed to them too little;

sentences.zh: 遍封萬戶，尚嫌恩疏。

translations.literal: enfeoffing ten thousand households everywhere, they still found favor sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Granting ten-thousand-household fiefs across the board they still deemed the grace insufficient.

sentences.zh: 茍思捧日之勤，遂據回天之勢。

translations.literal: If they reflected on the toil of holding up the sun, they then seized the power to turn heaven back.
translations.idiomatic: Once they fancied themselves sun-bearers to the throne, they claimed power to reverse heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 及三綱錯亂，四海崩離。

translations.literal: When the Three Bonds were disordered, the four seas collapsed and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When the fundamental bonds of society were overturned, the realm fell apart.

sentences.zh: 袁本初之入北宮，無須殆盡；

translations.literal: when Yuan Benchu entered the Northern Palace, the beardless were nearly exterminated;
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao stormed the Northern Palace, eunuchs were slaughtered almost to the last;

sentences.zh: 石冉閔之攻鄴下，內豎咸誅。

translations.literal: when Shi Ranmin attacked below Ye, inner attendants were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Min besieged Ye, every palace eunuch was killed.

sentences.zh: 旋至殄瘁邦家，不獨感傷和氣，淫刑斯逞，可為傷心。

translations.literal: Soon the state was wasted to exhaustion—not only harming harmonious qi; wanton punishments were unleashed—truly heartbreaking.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the state itself was brought to ruin—not merely harmony was wounded; lawless cruelty ran rampant, a grief to contemplate.

sentences.zh: 向使不假威權，但趨帷扆，何止四星終吉，抑亦萬乘延洪！

translations.literal: Had they not been lent authority but only hastened to the curtains and throne, how could it stop at the four stars ending auspiciously—they might also have extended the myriad carriages' grandeur!
translations.idiomatic: Had they never been lent power but only served at the throne's side, not only would the court have remained auspicious—the Son of Heaven's reign might have endured in splendor.

sentences.zh: 昔賢為社鼠之喻，不其然乎？

translations.literal: Ancient worthies made the parable of the temple rat—is it not so?
translations.idiomatic: The ancients compared them to rats in the temple altar—is it not exactly so?

sentences.zh: 今錄楊思勖已下所行事，以為鑒誡云。

translations.literal: Now I record the deeds of Yang Sixun and those below, to serve as warning and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Here I record the careers of Yang Sixun and those who follow, as a mirror and warning.

sentences.zh: =楊思勖=

translations.literal: = Yang Sixun =
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sixun

sentences.zh: 楊思勖，本姓蘇，羅州，石城人。

translations.literal: Yang Sixun, original surname Su, a native of Shicheng in Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sixun, born a Su of Shicheng in Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 為內官楊氏所養，以閹，從事內侍省。

translations.literal: He was reared by the inner official Lady Yang; he was castrated and served in the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch of the Yang clan adopted him; after castration he entered the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 預討李多祚功，超拜銀青光祿大夫，行內常侍。

translations.literal: He shared in the merit of campaigning against Li Duozuo and was promoted beyond norms to Silver-Glittering Blue-Luminous Grand Master, acting Inner Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For service in the campaign against Li Duozuo he was exceptionally promoted to Silver-Glittering Grand Master of the Palace and appointed acting Inner Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 思勖有膂力，殘忍好殺。

translations.literal: Sixun had physical strength and was cruel, delighting in killing.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun was powerfully built, cruel, and bloodthirsty.

sentences.zh: 從臨淄王誅韋氏，遂從王為爪士，累遷右監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Linzi in executing the Wei clan, then followed the prince as a claw warrior, rising through promotions to General of the Right Gate Guardian Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Linzi in the purge of the Wei faction, became one of the prince's fighting men, and rose to General of the Right Gate Guardian Guard.

sentences.zh: 開元初，安南首領梅玄成叛，自稱「黑帝」。

translations.literal: In early Kaiyuan the Annan chieftain Mei Xuancheng rebelled and styled himself "Black Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan the Annan leader Mei Xuancheng rebelled and proclaimed himself the Black Emperor.

sentences.zh: 與林邑、真臘國通謀，陷安南府。

translations.literal: He plotted with Linyi and Zhenla and seized Annan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Allying with Linyi and Cambodia he overran the protectorate of Annan.

sentences.zh: 詔思勖將兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sixun to lead troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Sixun to take command against him.

sentences.zh: 思勖至嶺表，鳩募首領子弟兵馬十餘萬，取伏波故道以進，出其不意。

translations.literal: Sixun reached the Lingnan region, gathered over a hundred thousand troops from chieftains' sons and younger brothers, advanced by Ma Yuan's old route, and struck by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the south, Sixun mustered more than a hundred thousand tribal levies, marched along Ma Yuan's ancient route, and caught the rebels unawares.

sentences.zh: 玄成遽聞兵至，惶惑計無所出，竟為官軍所擒，臨陣斬之，盡誅其黨與，積屍為京觀而還。

translations.literal: Xuancheng suddenly heard the army had arrived, was frightened and at a loss, and in the end was captured by government troops; he was beheaded on the field, all his partisans were executed, corpses were heaped into a victory mound, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng, hearing the army was upon him, panicked with no plan left; the government forces took him, slew him on the spot, wiped out his followers, piled the dead into a trophy mound, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 十二年，五溪首領覃行璋作亂，思勖復受詔率兵討之，生擒行璋，斬其黨三萬餘級。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Wuxi chieftain Qin Xingzhang rebelled; Sixun again received orders to lead troops against him, captured Xingzhang alive, and beheaded more than thirty thousand of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Qin Xingzhang of Wuxi rose in revolt; Sixun was again ordered to campaign, took Xingzhang alive, and slew more than thirty thousand of his band.

sentences.zh: 以軍功累加輔國大將軍。

translations.literal: For military merit he was repeatedly promoted to Grand General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: His battlefield merits won him repeated promotions to Grand General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 後從東封，又加驃騎大將軍，封虢國公。

translations.literal: Later he accompanied the eastern Feng sacrifice and was further made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and enfeoffed Duke of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He later attended the eastern Feng rites and was raised to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and created Duke of Guo.

sentences.zh: 十四年，邕州賊帥梁大海擁賓、橫等數州反叛。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the bandit chief of Yongzhou Liang Dahai held several prefectures including Bin and Heng and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Yongzhou rebel Liang Dahai seized several prefectures, including Bin and Heng, and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 思勖又統兵討之，生擒梁大海等三千餘人，斬餘黨二萬餘級，復積屍為京觀。

translations.literal: Sixun again commanded troops against him, captured Liang Dahai and more than three thousand alive, beheaded over twenty thousand remaining followers, and again heaped corpses into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun marched against him once more, took Liang Dahai and more than three thousand alive, slew over twenty thousand of their followers, and again raised a mound of heads.

sentences.zh: 十六年，瀧州首領陳行範、何遊魯、馮璘等聚徒作亂，陷四十餘城。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the Longzhou chieftains Chen Xingfan, He Youlu, Feng Lin, and others gathered followers and rebelled, taking over forty cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the Longzhou leaders Chen Xingfan, He Youlu, Feng Lin, and others raised troops in rebellion and captured more than forty towns.

sentences.zh: 行範自稱帝，遊魯稱定國大將軍，璘稱南越王，割據嶺表。

translations.literal: Xingfan styled himself emperor, Youlu styled himself Grand General Who Settles the State, Lin styled himself King of Southern Yue, and they carved up Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfan declared himself emperor, Youlu took the title Grand General Who Settles the State, Lin proclaimed himself King of Southern Yue, and together they held the Lingnan region.

sentences.zh: 詔思勖率永、連、道等兵及淮南弩手十萬人進討。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sixun to lead the armies of Yong, Lian, Dao, and others plus a hundred thousand crossbowmen from Huainan to advance and campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun was ordered to lead the Yong, Lian, and Dao forces and a hundred thousand Huainan crossbowmen against them.

sentences.zh: 兵至瀧州，臨陣擒遊魯、馮璘，斬之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Longzhou, on the field they captured Youlu and Feng Lin and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: At Longzhou his troops captured Youlu and Feng Lin in battle and executed them.

sentences.zh: 行範潛竄深州，投雲際、盤遼二洞。

translations.literal: Xingfan secretly fled into Shen prefecture and threw himself into the Yunji and Panliao caves.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfan slipped away into the deep hills of Shen prefecture and hid in the Yunji and Panliao cave strongholds.

sentences.zh: 思勖悉眾攻之，生擒行範，斬之。

translations.literal: Sixun brought his full force against him, captured Xingfan alive, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun attacked with his full strength, took Xingfan alive, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 斬其黨六萬級，獲口馬金玉巨萬計。

translations.literal: He beheaded sixty thousand of their followers; captives, horses, gold, and jade amounted to tens of thousands in tally.
translations.idiomatic: He slew sixty thousand rebels and seized captives, horses, gold, and jade beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 思勖性剛決，所得俘囚，多生剝其面，或剺發際，掣去頭皮；

translations.literal: Sixun was by nature stern and resolute; captives he took were often flayed alive on the face, or the hairline was cut and the scalp torn off;
translations.idiomatic: Sixun was ruthless by nature; prisoners were often flayed alive, or the scalp was torn from the hairline;

sentences.zh: 將士已下，望風懾憚，莫敢仰視，故所至立功。

translations.literal: officers and soldiers below looked to the wind in fear and did not dare look up—therefore wherever he went he achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: officers and men alike shrank from him in terror and dared not meet his gaze—hence his campaigns always succeeded.

sentences.zh: 內給事牛仙童使幽州，受張守珪厚賂。

translations.literal: The Inner Groom Niuxiantong was sent to Youzhou and received heavy bribes from Zhang Shougui.
translations.idiomatic: Niuxiantong, an inner chamberlain, was sent to Youzhou and accepted lavish bribes from Zhang Shougui.

sentences.zh: 玄宗怒，命思勖殺之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was angry and ordered Sixun to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong in a rage ordered Sixun to execute him.

sentences.zh: 思勖縛架之數日，乃探取其心，截去手足，割肉而啖之，其殘酷如此。

translations.literal: Sixun bound him on a rack for several days, then reached in and took his heart, cut off hands and feet, sliced flesh and ate it—his cruelty was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun bound him to a frame for days, then tore out his heart, hacked off his limbs, carved his flesh, and devoured it—such was his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 二十八年卒，時年八十餘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died, at over eighty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year, aged more than eighty.

sentences.zh: =高力士=

translations.literal: = Gao Lishi =
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi

sentences.zh: 高力士，潘州人，本姓馮。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi, a native of Panzhou, original surname Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi was a native of Panzhou; his birth surname was Feng.

sentences.zh: 少閹，與同類金剛二人，嶺南討擊使李千里進入宮。

translations.literal: Castrated young, he and two companions called Jingang were presented into the palace by the Lingnan Pacification Commissioner Li Qianli.
translations.idiomatic: Castrated in boyhood, he and two fellow eunuchs called Jingang were presented at court by the Lingnan commissioner Li Qianli.

sentences.zh: 則天嘉其黠惠，總角修整，令給事左右。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian admired his cleverness and grace; when his hair was bound in childhood she had him made orderly at her side.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu favored his sharp wit; she groomed him in his boyhood queue and assigned him to wait at her side.

sentences.zh: 後因小過，撻而逐之。

translations.literal: Later for a small fault he was flogged and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for a minor offense, he was whipped and driven out.

sentences.zh: 內官高延福收為假子。

translations.literal: The inner official Gao Yanfu took him as a foster son.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Gao Yanfu adopted him as a foster son.

sentences.zh: 延福出自武三思家，力士遂往來三思第。

translations.literal: Yanfu came from Wu Sansi's household, so Lishi then went back and forth to Sansi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfu had come from the household of Wu Sansi, and Lishi thus frequented Sansi's mansion.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，則天復召入禁中，隸司宮臺，廩食之。

translations.literal: After more than a year Wu Zetian recalled him into the inner palace, assigned him to the Palace Attendants Office, and gave him grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: After a year or more Wu Zetian summoned him back into the inner palace, enrolled him in the Palace Attendants Office, and provided his keep.

sentences.zh: 長六尺五寸，性謹密，能傳詔敕，授宮闈丞。

translations.literal: He was six feet five inches tall, cautious and discreet by nature, able to transmit edicts and rescripts, and was appointed Palace Inner Gate Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He stood six feet five inches, was discreet by nature, could convey imperial edicts, and was made deputy director of the inner palace gates.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，玄宗在籓，力士傾心奉之，接以恩顧。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era Xuanzong was in his princely fief; Lishi devoted his heart to serving him and was received with favor and regard.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong, while Xuanzong was still a prince, Lishi gave him his whole loyalty and was treated with personal favor.

sentences.zh: 及唐隆平內難，升儲位，奏力士屬內坊，日侍左右，擢授朝散大夫、內給事。

translations.literal: When the Tang pacified internal troubles and he ascended the heir's position, he memorialized that Lishi belong to the inner workshops, attend daily at his side, and was promoted to Grand Master of Leisurely Dispersal and Inner Groom.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty put down the inner strife and Xuanzong became heir apparent, he had Lishi assigned to the inner workshops to attend him daily, and promoted him to Grand Master of Leisurely Dispersal and inner chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 先天中，預誅蕭、岑等功，超拜銀青光祿大夫，行內侍同正員。

translations.literal: In the Xiantian era for sharing in the merit of executing Xiao, Cen, and others he was promoted beyond norms to Silver-Glittering Blue-Luminous Grand Master, acting Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantian, for his part in the execution of Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and their faction, he was raised to Silver-Glittering Grand Master and acting regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 開元初，加右監門衛將軍，知內侍省事。

translations.literal: In early Kaiyuan he was further made General of the Right Gate Guardian Guard and knew the affairs of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he was made General of the Right Gate Guardian Guard and placed in charge of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 玄宗尊重宮闈，中官稍稱旨，即授三品將軍，門施棨戟，故楊思勖、黎敬仁、林招隱、尹鳳祥等，貴寵與力士等。

translations.literal: Xuanzong honored the inner palace; inner officials who somewhat pleased him were immediately given third-rank general posts, with halberds at their gates—therefore Yang Sixun, Li Jingren, Lin Zhaoyin, Yin Fengxiang, and others enjoyed noble favor equal to Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong exalted the inner palace; any eunuch who pleased him might receive a third-rank generalship and halberds before his gate—thus Yang Sixun, Li Jingren, Lin Zhaoyin, Yin Fengxiang, and others shared Lishi's high favor.

sentences.zh: 楊則持節討伐，黎、林則奉使宣傳，尹則主書院。

translations.literal: Yang [Sixun] held credentials on punitive campaigns; Li and Lin were envoys for proclamation and transmission; Yin managed the academy of letters.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sixun led campaigns bearing imperial credentials; Li Jingren and Lin Zhaoyin served as envoys to announce imperial orders; Yin Fengxiang managed the palace academy.

sentences.zh: 其餘孫六、韓莊、楊八、牛仙童、劉奉廷、王承恩、張道斌、李大宜、硃光輝、郭全、邊令誠等，殿頭供奉、監軍、入蕃、教坊、功德主當，皆為委任之務。

translations.literal: Of the rest—Sun Liu, Han Zhuang, Yang Ba, Niu Xiantong, Liu Fengting, Wang Chengen, Zhang Daobin, Li Dayi, Zhu Guanghui, Guo Quan, Bian Lingcheng, and others—posts as hall-head attendants, army supervisors, envoys to Tibet, directors of the Music Office, and supervisors of merit works were all matters entrusted through them.
translations.idiomatic: The others—Sun Liu, Han Zhuang, Yang Ba, Niu Xiantong, Liu Fengting, Wang Chengen, Zhang Daobin, Li Dayi, Zhu Guanghui, Guo Quan, Bian Lingcheng, and the like—held posts as chief palace attendants, army supervisors, envoys to foreign lands, directors of the Music Office, and heads of merit-building projects; all such appointments flowed through them.

sentences.zh: 監軍則權過節度，出使則列郡辟易。

translations.literal: Army supervisors' authority surpassed that of military governors; when they went out on missions, commanderies cleared the way in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisors wielded more power than regional military governors, and when they traveled on missions the commanderies along the route yielded the road in alarm.

sentences.zh: 其郡縣豐贍，中官一至軍，則所冀千萬計，修功德，市鳥獸，詣一處，則不啻千貫，皆在力士可否。

translations.literal: In wealthy counties and districts, when eunuchs reached an army, what they sought ran into the tens of millions; building merit works, purchasing birds and beasts—to reach one place cost no less than a thousand strings of cash, all depending on whether Lishi approved.
translations.idiomatic: In prosperous counties and districts, when a eunuch arrived at an army camp his demands could run into the tens of millions; building merit shrines, buying birds and exotic beasts—a single visit cost no less than a thousand strings of cash, and all of it hinged on Lishi's approval.

sentences.zh: 故帝城中甲第，畿甸上田、果園池沼，中官參半於其間矣。

translations.literal: Thus within the imperial city, fine mansions, the capital district's best fields, orchards and ponds—eunuchs held half among them.
translations.idiomatic: Fine mansions in the imperial city, the best farmland in the capital region, orchards and ponds—eunuchs owned half of them.

sentences.zh: 每四方進奏文表，必先呈力士，然後進御，小事便決之。

translations.literal: Whenever memorial reports arrived from all quarters, they were first presented to Lishi, then forwarded to the emperor; minor matters he decided on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever memorials and reports arrived from the provinces, they were first shown to Lishi and only then forwarded to the emperor; on minor matters he decided at once.

sentences.zh: 玄宗常曰：「力士當上，我寢則穩。

translations.literal: Xuanzong often said: "When Lishi is stationed upstairs, my sleep is secure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong often said, "When Lishi is posted upstairs, I sleep soundly.

sentences.zh: 」故常止於宮中，稀出外宅。

translations.literal: " Therefore he regularly remained within the palace and rarely went to his outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: " So Lishi usually stayed in the palace and seldom visited his private residence outside.

sentences.zh: 若附會者，想望風彩，以冀吹噓，竭肝膽者多矣。

translations.literal: Those who sought to attach themselves to him, hoping for his reflected glory to gain promotion, poured out their hearts in numbers beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sought his patronage, hoping to bask in his reflected glory and win his recommendation, poured out their hearts in numbers beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 宇文融、李林甫、李適之、蓋嘉運、韋堅、楊慎矜、王鉷、楊國忠、安祿山、安思順、高仙芝因之而取將相高位，其餘職不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong, Li Linfu, Li Shizhi, Gai Jiayun, Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, Yang Guozhong, An Lushan, An Sishun, and Gao Xianzhi thereby obtained the high posts of generals and chancellors; the remaining offices are beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Through him Yuwen Rong, Li Linfu, Li Shizhi, Gai Jiayun, Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, Yang Guozhong, An Lushan, An Sishun, and Gao Xianzhi rose to the highest military and civil offices; the rest who gained posts through him are too many to record.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在春宮，呼為二兄，諸王公主皆呼「阿翁」，駙馬輩呼為「爺」。

translations.literal: When Suzong was in the Eastern Palace he called him Second Elder Brother; all princes and princesses called him "Grandfather"; sons-in-law called him "Sir."
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was crown prince he called Lishi Second Elder Brother; all princes and princesses called him "Grandfather"; the emperors' sons-in-law called him "Sir."

sentences.zh: 力士於寢殿側簾帷中休息，殿側亦有一院，中有修功德處，雕瑩璀璨，窮極精妙。

translations.literal: Lishi rested in the curtained alcove beside the sleeping hall; beside the hall there was also a courtyard with a place for merit works, carved and inlaid in dazzling brilliance to the utmost refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi rested in the curtained alcove beside the imperial sleeping hall; there was also a courtyard beside the hall with a chapel for merit-building, carved and inlaid with dazzling brilliance to the highest degree of craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 力士謹慎無大過，然自宇文融已下，用權相噬，以紊朝綱，皆力士之由。

translations.literal: Lishi was cautious and made no great errors, yet from Yuwen Rong downward, those who wielded power devoured one another and disrupted court order—all stemming from Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi was careful and committed no major fault, yet from Yuwen Rong on down, those who wielded power tore one another apart and threw the court into disorder—and all of it traced back to Lishi.

sentences.zh: 又與時消息，觀其勢候，雖至親愛，臨覆敗皆不之救。

translations.literal: He also tracked the times and watched the tides of fortune; even for those closest to him, when ruin came he never rescued them.
translations.idiomatic: He also kept abreast of the times and watched how the wind was blowing; even those dearest to him, when disaster struck, he never saved.

sentences.zh: 力士義父高延福夫妻，正授供奉。

translations.literal: Lishi's adoptive father Gao Yanfu and his wife were given regular appointments as palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi's adoptive father Gao Yanfu and his wife were formally appointed palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使於潘州求其本母麥氏送長安，令兩媼在堂，備於甘脆。

translations.literal: The Lingnan military governor sought out his biological mother Lady Mai at Pan Prefecture and sent her to Chang'an; two old nurses attended her in the hall, supplied with delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor of Lingnan found his birth mother Lady Mai at Pan Prefecture and sent her to Chang'an; two old nurses waited on her in the hall and she was provided with every delicacy.

sentences.zh: 金吾大將軍程伯獻與力士結為兄弟，麥氏亡，伯獻於靈筵散發，具缞绖，受賓吊答。

translations.literal: The Gold Guard Grand General Cheng Boxian formed a sworn brotherhood with Lishi; when Lady Mai died, Boxian at the mourning hall loosened his hair, wore hemp mourning garments, and received guests' condolences on her behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The Gold Guard Grand General Cheng Boxian became sworn brothers with Lishi; when Lady Mai died, Boxian at the mourning hall let down his hair, put on hemp mourning dress, and received condolences from guests on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 十七年，贈力士父廣州大都督，麥氏越國夫人。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year [729], Lishi's father was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Guangzhou and Lady Mai Lady of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan, Lishi's father was posthumously enfeoffed as Metropolitan Governor of Guangzhou and Lady Mai as Lady of Yue.

sentences.zh: 開元初，瀛州呂玄晤作吏京師，女有姿色，力士娶之為婦，擢玄晤為少卿、刺史，子弟皆為王傅。

translations.literal: In early Kaiyuan, Lu Xuanwu of Ying Prefecture served as a clerk in the capital; his daughter was beautiful, and Lishi married her; Xuanwu was promoted to vice minister and governor, and his sons and younger kinsmen all became tutors to princes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, Lu Xuanwu of Ying Prefecture was a clerk in the capital; his daughter was beautiful, and Lishi married her; Xuanwu was promoted to vice minister and regional governor, and his sons and nephews all became tutors to imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 呂夫人卒，葬城東，葬禮甚盛。

translations.literal: When Lady Lu died, she was buried east of the city in a very grand funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Lu died, she was buried east of the city in an exceptionally grand funeral.

sentences.zh: 中外爭致祭贈，充溢衢路；

translations.literal: Officials inside and outside the court competed to send sacrificial offerings and gifts, filling the streets;
translations.idiomatic: Officials inside and outside the court vied to send funeral offerings and gifts until the streets overflowed;

sentences.zh: 自第至墓，車馬不絕。

translations.literal: From the mansion to the tomb, carriages and horses never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: from the mansion to the tomb, carriages and horses never stopped passing.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，加力士冠軍大將軍、右監門衛大將軍，進封渤海郡公。

translations.literal: In early Tianbao, Lishi was further made Champion Grand General and Grand General of the Right Gate Guardian Guard, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao, Lishi was further promoted to Champion Grand General and Grand General of the Right Gate Guardian Guard, and raised in rank to Duke of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 七載，加驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year [748], he was further made Flying Cavalry Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianbao he was further made Flying Cavalry Grand General.

sentences.zh: 力士資產殷厚，非王侯能擬。

translations.literal: Lishi's assets were immense, beyond what kings and marquises could match.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi's wealth was vast, beyond anything kings and marquises could rival.

sentences.zh: 於來庭坊造寶壽佛寺、興寧坊造華封道士觀，寶殿珍臺，侔於國力。

translations.literal: At Laiting Ward he built Baoshou Buddhist Temple; at Xingning Ward he built Huafeng Daoist Abbey—precious halls and jeweled terraces rivaling the state's resources.
translations.idiomatic: At Laiting Ward he built Baoshou Buddhist Temple, and at Xingning Ward he built Huafeng Daoist Abbey; their jeweled halls and precious terraces rivaled the resources of the state itself.

sentences.zh: 於京城西北截澧水作碾，並轉五輪，日破麥三百斛。

translations.literal: Northwest of the capital he diverted the Li River to drive a mill with five wheels, grinding three hundred hu of wheat daily.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of the capital he diverted the Li River to power a mill with five wheels, grinding three hundred hu of wheat each day.

sentences.zh: 初，寶壽寺鐘成，力士齋慶之，舉朝畢至。

translations.literal: When the Baoshou Temple bell was first cast, Lishi held a fasting celebration; the whole court attended.
translations.idiomatic: When the Baoshou Temple bell was first cast, Lishi held a fasting celebration for it, and the entire court came.

sentences.zh: 凡擊鐘者，一擊百千；

translations.literal: Everyone who struck the bell gave a hundred or a thousand [cash per blow];
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who struck the bell gave a hundred or a thousand cash per blow;

sentences.zh: 有規其意者，擊至二十杵，少尚十杵。

translations.literal: Those who disapproved of the extravagance struck up to twenty blows; none gave fewer than ten.
translations.idiomatic: those who disapproved of the extravagance still struck as many as twenty blows; none gave fewer than ten.

sentences.zh: 其後又有華州袁思藝，特承恩顧。

translations.literal: Later there was also Yuan Siyi of Hua Prefecture, who enjoyed special imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was also Yuan Siyi of Hua Prefecture, who received special imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 然力士巧密，人悅之；

translations.literal: Yet Lishi was tactful and subtle, and people liked him;
translations.idiomatic: But Lishi was tactful and discreet, and people liked him;

sentences.zh: 思藝驕倨，人士疏懼之。

translations.literal: Siyi was arrogant and haughty, and officials kept their distance and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Siyi was arrogant and overbearing, and officials kept their distance and feared him.

sentences.zh: 十四載，置內侍省內侍監兩員，秩正三品，以力士、思藝對任之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year [755], two posts of Inner Attendant Supervisor of third rank were established in the Palace Domestic Service; Lishi and Siyi were appointed as a pair.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao two posts of Inner Attendant Supervisor at the third rank were established in the Palace Domestic Service, and Lishi and Siyi were appointed to them as a pair.

sentences.zh: 玄宗幸蜀，思藝走投祿山，力士從幸成都，進封齊國公。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong fled to Shu, Siyi fled to join An Lushan; Lishi accompanied the emperor to Chengdu and was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled to Shu, Siyi fled to An Lushan; Lishi accompanied the emperor to Chengdu and was raised in rank to Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 從上皇還京，加開府儀同三司，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital with the Retired Emperor, he was given the status of Grand Master with Golden Tally opening his own office, with five hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital with the Retired Emperor, he was granted the status of Grand Master with Golden Tally opening his own office and given five hundred households of actual fief.

sentences.zh: 八月，上皇移居西內甘露殿，力士與內官王承恩、魏悅等，因侍上皇登長慶樓，為李輔國所構，配流黔中道。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Retired Emperor moved to Ganlu Hall in the Western Inner Palace; Lishi, together with the inner officials Wang Chengen, Wei Yue, and others, while attending the Retired Emperor as he ascended Changqing Tower, was framed by Li Fuguo and sentenced to exile on the Qianzhong route.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Retired Emperor moved to Ganlu Hall in the Western Inner Palace; Lishi, along with the eunuchs Wang Chengen, Wei Yue, and others, while attending the Retired Emperor on Changqing Tower, was framed by Li Fuguo and sentenced to exile on the Qianzhong circuit.

sentences.zh: 力士至巫州，地多薺而不食，因感傷而詠之曰：「兩京作芹賣，五溪無人采。

translations.literal: When Lishi reached Wuzhou, the land had much shepherd's purse but he did not eat it; moved to sadness he composed and recited: "In the two capitals, celery is sold; in the Five Streams, none gathers it.
translations.idiomatic: When Lishi reached Wuzhou, shepherd's purse grew everywhere but he would not eat it; grief-stricken, he composed a poem: "In the two capitals, water celery is sold for coin; along the Five Streams, no one picks it.

sentences.zh: 夷夏雖不同，氣味終不改。

translations.literal: Though barbarian lands and China differ, the flavor in the end does not change.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian and Han lands may differ, yet its taste in the end never alters.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年三月，會赦歸，至朗州，遇流人言京國事，始知上皇厭代。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Baoying [762], when a general amnesty was proclaimed he was allowed to return; reaching Lang Prefecture, he met exiles who spoke of capital affairs and first learned that the Retired Emperor had passed away.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Baoying, when a general amnesty was proclaimed he was permitted to return; at Lang Prefecture he met exiles who spoke of affairs in the capital and first learned that the Retired Emperor had died.

sentences.zh: 力士北望號慟，嘔血而卒。

translations.literal: Lishi looked north and wailed in grief, spat blood, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi looked north and wailed in grief, vomited blood, and died.

sentences.zh: 代宗以其耆宿，保護先朝，贈揚州大都督，陪葬泰陵。

translations.literal: Daizong, because of his seniority and his service protecting the former reign, posthumously made him Metropolitan Governor of Yangzhou and granted burial at Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong, because of his long service and his protection of the former reign, posthumously enfeoffed him as Metropolitan Governor of Yangzhou and granted him burial at Tailing.

sentences.zh: =李輔國=

translations.literal: = Li Fuguo =
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo

sentences.zh: 李輔國，本名靜忠，閑廄馬家小兒。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo, original name Jingzhong, was a groom-boy in the imperial stud farms.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo, whose original name was Jingzhong, was a groom-boy in the imperial stud farms.

sentences.zh: 少為閹，貌陋，粗知書計。

translations.literal: Castrated young, ugly in appearance, he had a rough knowledge of writing and accounting.
translations.idiomatic: He was castrated in youth, was ugly in appearance, and had a rough knowledge of writing and bookkeeping.

sentences.zh: 為僕，事高力士，年且四十餘，令掌廄中簿籍。

translations.literal: Serving as a servant under Gao Lishi, when he was over forty he was ordered to manage the stud farm ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: As a servant under Gao Lishi, when he was over forty he was put in charge of the stud farm ledgers.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，閑廄使五鉷嘉其畜牧之能，薦入東宮。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, Wang Hong, Commissioner of the Imperial Stud, admired his skill in animal husbandry and recommended him to enter the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao, Wang Hong, Commissioner of the Imperial Stud, admired his skill in animal husbandry and recommended him for service in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，玄宗幸蜀；

translations.literal: When An Lushan's rebellion broke out, Xuanzong fled to Shu;
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan's rebellion broke out, Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu;

sentences.zh: 輔國侍太子扈從，至馬嵬，誅楊國忠。

translations.literal: Fuguo attended the Crown Prince in the imperial retinue; at Mawei they executed Yang Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo attended the crown prince in the imperial retinue; at Mawei Yang Guozhong was executed.

sentences.zh: 輔國獻計太子，請分玄宗麾下兵，北趨朔方，以圖興復。

translations.literal: Fuguo proposed to the Crown Prince that they detach troops from Xuanzong's command and march north toward Shuofang to plan restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo advised the crown prince to detach troops from Xuanzong's command and march north toward Shuofang to plan the restoration of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 輔國從至靈武，勸太子即帝位，以系人心。

translations.literal: Fuguo followed on to Lingwu and urged the Crown Prince to take the throne immediately to secure popular loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo followed on to Lingwu and urged the crown prince to ascend the throne at once to secure the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，擢為太子家令，判元帥府行軍司馬事，以心腹委之。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, Fuguo was promoted to Director of the Crown Prince's Household and concurrent Chief of Staff of the Marshal's headquarters, entrusted as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong ascended the throne, Fuguo was promoted to Director of the Crown Prince's Household and made concurrent Chief of Staff of the Marshal's headquarters, entrusted as a close confidant.

sentences.zh: 仍賜名護國，四方奏事，御前符印軍號，一以委之。

translations.literal: He was also granted the name Huguo; memorials from all quarters, imperial seals and tally codes before the throne, and military designations were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted the name Huguo; memorials from all quarters, imperial seals and tallies before the throne, and military designations were all entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 輔國不茹葷血，常為僧行，視事之隙，手持念珠，人皆信以為善。

translations.literal: Fuguo ate no meat and often went about as a monk; in intervals between handling affairs he held prayer beads, and people all believed him good.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo abstained from meat and often went about dressed as a monk; in intervals between handling business he held prayer beads, and everyone believed him virtuous.

sentences.zh: 從幸鳳翔，授太子詹事，改名輔國。

translations.literal: When Suzong went to Fengxiang he was appointed Grand Steward of the Crown Prince and renamed Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong went to Fengxiang, Fuguo was appointed Grand Steward of the Crown Prince and renamed Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 肅宗還京，拜殿中監，閑廄、五坊、宮苑、營田、栽接、總監等使。

translations.literal: When Suzong returned to the capital he was made Director of the Palace Bureau and commissioner for the imperial stud, Five Wards, palace gardens, military farming colonies, grafting plantations, and overall supervision.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong returned to the capital, Fuguo was made Director of the Palace Bureau and commissioner of the imperial stud, Five Wards, palace gardens, military farming colonies, grafting plantations, and overall supervision.

sentences.zh: 又兼隴右群牧、京畿鑄錢、長春宮等使，勾當少府、殿中二監都使。

translations.literal: He also concurrently held the posts of Commissioner of Longyou Herds, Commissioner of Capital Region Coinage, Commissioner of Chunzhang Palace, and overall manager of the offices of the Imperial Manufactories and Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He also concurrently served as Commissioner of Longyou Herds, Commissioner of Capital Region Coinage, Commissioner of Chunzhang Palace, and overall manager of the Imperial Manufactories and Palace Bureau.

sentences.zh: 十二月，加開府儀同三司，進封郕國公，食實封五百戶。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was given the status of Grand Master with Golden Tally opening his own office, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Bi, with five hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was granted the status of Grand Master with Golden Tally opening his own office, raised to Duke of Bi, and given five hundred households of actual fief.

sentences.zh: 宰臣百司，不時奏事，皆因輔國上決。

translations.literal: Chancellors and the hundred offices, when they did not appear at court to memorial, all submitted decisions through Fuguo to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When chancellors and the hundred offices did not appear at court to memorialize, all business was submitted through Fuguo for the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 常在銀臺門受事，置察事廳子數十人，官吏有小過，無不伺知，即加推訊。

translations.literal: He regularly received business at Silver Terrace Gate; he set up investigative hall agents numbering in the tens, and no minor fault of an official escaped their notice—they immediately interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly received business at Silver Terrace Gate; he stationed dozens of investigative agents, and no minor fault of an official escaped their notice—they at once subjected him to interrogation.

sentences.zh: 府縣按鞫，三司制獄，必詣輔國取決，隨意區分，皆稱制敕，無敢異議者。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county trials, and the Three Offices' criminal cases, all had to go to Fuguo for final judgment; he disposed of them as he pleased, all in the name of imperial edicts, and none dared dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county trials and cases under the Three Offices' criminal jurisdiction all had to go to Fuguo for final judgment; he disposed of them as he pleased, all in the name of imperial edicts, and no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 每出則甲士數百人衛從。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out, several hundred armored soldiers escorted him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went out, several hundred armored soldiers escorted him.

sentences.zh: 中貴人不敢呼其官，但呼五郎。

translations.literal: Inner favorites did not dare call him by his office title but only called him Fifth Master.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow eunuchs did not dare call him by his official title but only called him Fifth Master.

sentences.zh: 宰相李揆，山東甲族，位居臺輔，見輔國執子弟之禮，謂之五父。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Kui, of an eminent Shandong clan, held the highest ministerial rank; seeing Fuguo he performed the rites of a junior kinsman and addressed him as Fifth Father.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Kui, of an eminent Shandong clan and the highest ministerial rank, performed the rites of a junior kinsman toward Fuguo and addressed him as Fifth Father.

sentences.zh: 肅宗又為輔國娶故吏部侍郎元希聲侄擢女為妻。

translations.literal: Suzong also arranged a marriage for Fuguo with the daughter of Zhi, nephew of former Vice Minister of Personnel Yuan Xisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong also arranged for Fuguo to marry the daughter of Zhi, nephew of the former Vice Minister of Personnel Yuan Xisheng.

sentences.zh: 擢弟挹，時並引入臺省，擢為梁州長史。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Yi was then also brought into the central ministries; Yi was made long prefect of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Yi was then also brought into the central ministries; Yi was made long prefect of Liang.

sentences.zh: 輔國判元帥行軍司馬，專掌禁兵，賜內宅居止。

translations.literal: Fuguo, as Chief of Staff of the Marshal's headquarters, exclusively held the forbidden army; he was granted a residence within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: As Chief of Staff of the Marshal's headquarters, Fuguo exclusively controlled the forbidden army and was granted a residence within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 上皇自蜀還京，居興慶宮，肅宗自夾城中起居。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor returned from Shu to the capital he lived at Xingqing Palace; Suzong resided within the walled inner compound.
translations.idiomatic: When the Retired Emperor returned from Shu to the capital he lived at Xingqing Palace; Suzong resided in the walled inner compound.

sentences.zh: 上皇時召伶官奏樂，持盈公主往來宮中，輔國常陰候其隙而間之。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor would summon musicians; Princess Chi-ying came and went in the palace; Fuguo often secretly watched for openings to sow discord.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor would summon musicians to perform; Princess Chi-ying came and went within the palace; Fuguo often secretly watched for openings to sow discord.

sentences.zh: ，上皇嘗登長慶樓，與公主語。

translations.literal: Once the Retired Emperor ascended Changqing Tower and spoke with the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Retired Emperor ascended Changqing Tower and spoke with the princess.

sentences.zh: 劍南奏事官過朝謁，上皇令公主及如仙媛作主人。

translations.literal: A reporting official from Jiannan passed by on court audience; the Retired Emperor had the princess and Lady Ru-xianyuan act as hosts.
translations.idiomatic: A reporting official from Jiannan passed by on his way to court audience; the Retired Emperor had the princess and Lady Ru-xianyuan act as hosts.

sentences.zh: 輔國起微賤，貴達日近，不為上皇左右所禮，慮恩顧或衰，乃潛畫奇謀以自固。

translations.literal: Fuguo rose from humble origins; as his rank grew daily closer, the Retired Emperor's attendants did not treat him with courtesy; fearing imperial favor might fade, he secretly devised extraordinary plots to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo had risen from humble origins; as his rank drew ever closer to power, the Retired Emperor's attendants did not treat him with courtesy; fearing that imperial favor might wane, he secretly devised extraordinary schemes to secure his position.

sentences.zh: 因持盈待客，乃奏云：「南內有異謀。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of Chi-ying receiving guests, he memorialized: "There is a subversive plot in the Southern Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Taking advantage of Chi-ying's reception of guests, he memorialized: "There is a subversive plot in the Southern Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 」矯詔移上皇居西內，送持盈於玉真觀，高力士等皆坐流竄。

translations.literal: " By forged edict the Retired Emperor was moved to the Western Inner Palace; Chi-ying was sent to Yuzhen Abbey; Gao Lishi and the others were all sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: " By forged edict the Retired Emperor was moved to the Western Inner Palace; Chi-ying was sent to Yuzhen Abbey; Gao Lishi and the others were all sentenced to exile.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，拜兵部尚書，餘官如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year [757] he was made Minister of War; other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year he was appointed Minister of War; his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣於尚書省送上，賜御府酒饌、太常樂，武士戎服夾道，朝列畢會。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to escort him at the Ministry of War; he was granted wine and food from the imperial kitchen and music from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; armored warriors in military garb lined the road; the full court assembled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ministers to escort him at the Ministry of War; he was granted wine and food from the imperial kitchen and music from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; warriors in military dress lined both sides of the road, and the full court assembled.

sentences.zh: 輔國驕恣日甚，求為宰臣，肅宗曰：「以公勛力，何官不可，但未允朝望，如何？

translations.literal: Fuguo's arrogance grew daily; he sought to become a chancellor. Suzong said: "Given your merit, what office could you not hold? But it would not satisfy court opinion—what then?
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo's arrogance grew daily; he sought to become a chancellor. Suzong said, "Given your merit, what office could you not hold? But it would not satisfy court opinion—what then?

sentences.zh: 」輔國諷僕射裴冕聯章薦己。

translations.literal: " Fuguo prompted Vice Director Pei Mian to submit a joint memorial recommending himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Fuguo prompted Vice Director Pei Mian to submit a joint memorial recommending him for chancellor.

sentences.zh: 肅宗密謂宰臣蕭華曰：「輔國欲帶平章事，卿等欲有章薦，信乎？

translations.literal: Suzong secretly told Chancellor Xiao Hua: "Fuguo wishes to carry the title of Co-director of the Department of State Affairs; do you intend to submit a memorial recommending him—is that true?
translations.idiomatic: Suzong secretly told Chancellor Xiao Hua, "Fuguo wishes to carry the title of Co-director of the Department of State Affairs; do you intend to submit a memorial recommending him—is that true?

sentences.zh: 」華不對。

translations.literal: " Hua did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Hua did not reply.

sentences.zh: 問裴冕，曰：「初無此事，吾臂可截，宰相不可得也。

translations.literal: Asked Pei Mian, who said: "There is nothing of the sort at first; my arm may be cut off—the post of chancellor cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Pei Mian, who said, "There is nothing of the sort; my arm may be cut off—the post of chancellor cannot be obtained.

sentences.zh: 」華復入奏，上喜曰：「冕固堪大用。

translations.literal: " Hua entered again to memorialize; the emperor said with delight: "Mian is indeed fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: " Hua entered again to memorialize; the emperor said with delight, "Mian is indeed fit for great employment.

sentences.zh: 」輔國銜之。

translations.literal: " Fuguo harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: " Fuguo harbored resentment against him.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年四月，肅宗寢疾，宰臣等不可謁見，輔國誣奏華專權，請黜之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Baoying [762], Suzong was gravely ill and the chancellors could not be received in audience; Fuguo falsely memorialized that Xiao Hua monopolized authority and requested his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Baoying, Suzong was gravely ill and the chancellors could not be received in audience; Fuguo falsely memorialized that Xiao Hua monopolized authority and requested his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 上不許，輔國固請不已。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree, but Fuguo repeatedly insisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree, but Fuguo repeatedly pressed his request.

sentences.zh: 乃罷華知政事，守禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Xiao Hua was then removed from handling state affairs and retained only as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hua was then removed from handling state affairs and retained only as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，華竟被斥逐。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Xiao Hua was ultimately driven out and banished.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Xiao Hua was ultimately driven out and banished.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，輔國與程元振有定策功，愈恣橫。

translations.literal: When Daizong ascended the throne, Fuguo and Cheng Yuanzhen had merit in settling the succession and became ever more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong ascended the throne, Fuguo and Cheng Yuanzhen had merit in settling the succession and became ever more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 私奏曰：「大家但內裏坐，外事聽老奴處置。

translations.literal: In a private memorial he said: "Your Majesty need only sit within the inner palace; outer affairs let this old slave handle.
translations.idiomatic: In a private memorial he said, "Your Majesty need only sit within the inner palace; let this old slave handle outer affairs.

sentences.zh: 」代宗怒其不遜，以方握禁軍，不欲遽責。

translations.literal: " Daizong was angered at his insubordination, but because Fuguo still controlled the forbidden army he did not wish to rebuke him hastily.
translations.idiomatic: " Daizong was angered at his insubordination, but because Fuguo still controlled the forbidden army he did not wish to rebuke him hastily.

sentences.zh: 乃尊為尚父，政無巨細，皆委參決。

translations.literal: He was then honored as Imperial Father; no matter how great or small, all government affairs were entrusted to him for joint decision.
translations.idiomatic: He was then honored as Imperial Father; matters great and small were all entrusted to him for joint decision.

sentences.zh: 五月，加司空、中書令，食實封八百戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was further made Minister of Works and Grand Secretary of the Secretariat, with eight hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was further made Minister of Works and Grand Secretary of the Secretariat, with eight hundred households of actual fief.

sentences.zh: 程元振欲奪其權，請上漸加禁制，乘其有間，乃罷輔國判元帥行軍事，其閑廄已下使名，並分授諸貴，仍移居外。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanzhen wished to seize his power and requested that the emperor gradually impose restrictions; seizing an opportunity, Fuguo's concurrent post as Chief of Staff of the Marshal's headquarters was removed, his commissions from the imperial stud downward were all divided among various favorites, and he was still moved to live outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen wished to seize his power and asked the emperor to gradually impose restrictions; seizing an opportunity, he removed Fuguo's concurrent post as Chief of Staff of the Marshal's headquarters, divided his commissions from the imperial stud downward among various favorites, and moved him to live outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 輔國始懼，茫然失據。

translations.literal: Fuguo began to fear; he was dazed and lost his footing.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo began to fear; he was dazed and lost his footing.

sentences.zh: 詔進封博陸王，罷中書令，許朝朔望。

translations.literal: An edict advanced his enfeoffment to Prince of Bolu, removed him as Grand Secretary, and permitted him to attend court on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: An edict advanced his enfeoffment to Prince of Bolu, removed him as Grand Secretary, and permitted him to attend court on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 輔國欲入中書修謝表，閽吏止之曰：「尚父罷相，不合復入此門。

translations.literal: Fuguo wished to enter the Secretariat to draft a letter of thanks; the gatekeeper stopped him, saying: "The Imperial Father has been removed as chancellor; it is not permitted to enter this gate again.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo wished to enter the Secretariat to draft a letter of thanks; the gatekeeper stopped him, saying, "The Imperial Father has been removed as chancellor; it is not permitted to enter this gate again.

sentences.zh: 」乃氣憤而言曰：「老奴死罪，事朗君不了，請於地下事先帝。

translations.literal: " He then spoke in indignant fury: "This old slave deserves death—I have failed to serve Lord Lang; I beg to go below to serve the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " He then spoke in indignant fury, "This old slave deserves death—I have failed to serve Lord Lang; I beg to go below and serve the former emperor.

sentences.zh: 」上猶優詔答之。

translations.literal: " The emperor still answered with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor still answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 十月十八日夜，盜入輔國第，殺輔國，攜首臂而去。

translations.literal: On the night of the eighteenth day of the tenth month, thieves broke into Fuguo's residence, killed him, and carried off his head and arm.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the eighteenth day of the tenth month, thieves broke into Fuguo's residence, killed him, and carried off his head and arm.

sentences.zh: 詔刻木首葬之，仍贈太傅。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that a wooden head be carved for burial, and he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a wooden replica of his head carved for burial, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: =程元振=

translations.literal: = Cheng Yuanzhen =
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen

sentences.zh: 程元振，以宦者直內侍省，累遷至內射生使。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanzhen, as a eunuch serving in the Palace Domestic Service, was promoted repeatedly until he became Commissioner of the Inner Archery Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen entered the Palace Domestic Service as a eunuch and rose through successive postings until he became Commissioner of the Inner Archery Guard.

sentences.zh: 寶應末，肅宗晏駕，張皇后與太子有怨，恐不附己，引越王系入宮，欲令監國。

translations.literal: At the end of the Baoying era, when Suzong died peacefully, Empress Zhang bore a grudge against the Crown Prince and, fearing he would not align with her, brought the Prince of Yue, Li Xi, into the palace and wished to have him oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Baoying era, when Emperor Suzong died, Empress Zhang, who was at odds with the Crown Prince, feared he would not support her. She summoned the Prince of Yue, Li Xi, into the palace and sought to install him as regent.

sentences.zh: 元振知其謀，密告李輔國，乃挾太子，誅越王並其黨與。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen learned of the plot, secretly informed Li Fuguo, then seized the Crown Prince, executed the Prince of Yue together with his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen learned of the plot and secretly informed Li Fuguo. They then secured the Crown Prince, executed the Prince of Yue, and destroyed his faction.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，以功拜飛龍副使、右監門將軍、上柱國，知內侍省事。

translations.literal: When Daizong ascended the throne, for his merit he was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Flying Dragon Guard, General of the Right Gate Guards, Supreme Pillar of State, and acting Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong took the throne, Yuanzhen was rewarded for his service with appointments as Deputy Commissioner of the Flying Dragon Guard, General of the Right Gate Guards, Supreme Pillar of State, and acting Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 尋代輔國判元帥行軍司馬，專制禁兵，加鎮軍大將軍、右監門衛大將軍，封保定縣侯，充寶應軍使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he replaced Fuguo as concurrent Chief of Staff of the Marshal's headquarters, monopolized control of the forbidden army, was further made General of Garrisoned Armies and Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Baoding County, and appointed Commissioner of the Baoying Army.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Fuguo as concurrent chief of staff of the imperial field headquarters and assumed sole control of the palace armies. He was further promoted to General of Garrisoned Armies and Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Baoding County, and made commissioner of the Baoying Army.

sentences.zh: 九月，加驃騎大將軍，封邠國公，贈其父元貞司空。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was further made General of Fast Cavalry, enfeoffed as Duke of Bin, and his father Yuan Zhen was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was further promoted to General of Fast Cavalry and enfeoffed as Duke of Bin; his father Yuan Zhen was posthumously granted Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 母郤氏，趙國夫人。

translations.literal: His mother was the Lady of Zhao, née Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Xi, granted the title Lady of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 是時元振之權，甚於輔國，軍中呼為「十郎」。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanzhen's power exceeded Fuguo's; in the army he was called "Tenth Son."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuanzhen wielded greater power than Fuguo, and the army called him "Tenth Son."

sentences.zh: 元振常請托於襄陽節度使來瑱，瑱不從。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen often solicited favors from the military commissioner of Xiangyang, Lai Tian, but Lai would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen often pressed the military commissioner of Xiangyang, Lai Tian, for favors, but Lai refused.

sentences.zh: 及元振握權，征瑱入朝。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhen seized power, he summoned Lai Tian to court.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuanzhen held power, he summoned Lai Tian to court.

sentences.zh: 瑱遷延不至。

translations.literal: Lai delayed and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian delayed and did not come.

sentences.zh: ，破裴茙，遂入朝，拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Having defeated Pei Ji, he then came to court and was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Pei Ji, he finally came to court and was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 元振欲報私憾，誣瑱之罪，竟坐誅。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen wished to settle a private grudge; he framed Lai with false charges, and Lai was ultimately executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen wished to settle a private score. He framed Lai Tian with false charges, and Lai was ultimately executed.

sentences.zh: 宰臣裴冕為肅宗山陵使，有事與元振相違，乃發小吏贓私，貶冕施州刺史。

translations.literal: Chancellor Pei Mian served as commissioner for Suzong's tomb; when something conflicted with Yuanzhen, Yuanzhen exposed petty clerks' embezzlements and had Pei Mian demoted to prefect of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Pei Mian, who oversaw Emperor Suzong's tomb, clashed with Yuanzhen on a matter. Yuanzhen exposed petty clerks' embezzlements and had Pei Mian demoted to prefect of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 來瑱名將，裴冕元勛，二人既被誣陷，天下方鎮皆解體。

translations.literal: Lai Tian was a renowned general and Pei Mian a founding merit-holder; once both had been falsely implicated, all the regional commands throughout the realm lost cohesion.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian was a celebrated general and Pei Mian a founding merit-holder. Once both had been framed, military governors across the empire lost heart.

sentences.zh: 元振猶以驕豪自處，不顧物議。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen still conducted himself with arrogant bravado, heedless of public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen still carried himself with arrogant swagger, heedless of public criticism.

sentences.zh: 九月，吐蕃、党項入犯京畿，下詔征兵，諸道卒無至者。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Tibetans and Tangut forces invaded the capital region; an edict conscripted troops, but from none of the circuits did soldiers arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Tibetan and Tangut forces invaded the capital region. Though an edict called up troops, not a man arrived from any circuit.

sentences.zh: 十月，蕃軍至便橋，代宗蒼黃出幸陜州；

translations.literal: In the tenth month the barbarian army reached Bian Bridge; Daizong fled in panic to Shanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the enemy army reached Bian Bridge, and Emperor Daizong fled in haste to Shanzhou;

sentences.zh: 賊陷京師，府庫蕩盡。

translations.literal: The rebels took the capital, and the treasuries were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy seized the capital, and the imperial treasuries were stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 及至行在，太常博士柳伉上疏切諫誅元振以謝天下，代宗顧人情歸咎，乃罷元振官，放歸田裏，家在三原。

translations.literal: When they reached the temporary court, Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Liu Kang submitted a memorial urgently remonstrating that Yuanzhen be executed to appease the realm. Daizong, considering that popular sentiment blamed him, removed Yuanzhen from office and sent him back to his fields; his home was in Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the court reached its temporary seat at Shanzhou, Liu Kang, a doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, submitted an urgent memorial calling for Yuanzhen's execution to appease the realm. Seeing that public blame fell on Yuanzhen, Daizong stripped him of office and sent him back to his estate at Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，車駕還京。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 元振服缞麻於車中，入京城，以規任用。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen wore hemp mourning garb in his carriage and entered the capital city, seeking to maneuver himself back into appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen rode into the capital wearing coarse hemp mourning garb, hoping to win reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 與御史大夫王昇飲酒，為御史所彈。

translations.literal: He drank wine with Censor-in-Chief Wang Sheng and was impeached by the censors.
translations.idiomatic: He drank wine with Censor-in-Chief Wang Sheng and was impeached by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict declared:
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared:

sentences.zh: 族談錯立，法尚不容；

translations.literal: "When Chao Cuo's entire clan was executed for his installation in power, the law still could not tolerate it;
translations.idiomatic: "When Chao Cuo's entire clan was put to death for his elevation to power, the law still could not countenance it;

sentences.zh: 同惡陰謀，議當從重。

translations.literal: Those who share in evil conspiracies, when deliberated upon, should receive the heavier penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Those who join in secret conspiracies should, upon deliberation, receive the heavier penalty.

sentences.zh: 有一於此，情實難原。

translations.literal: Where any one of these applies, the circumstances truly admit no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Where either applies, the circumstances truly admit no pardon.

sentences.zh: 程元振性惟兇愎，質本庸愚，蕞爾之身，合當萬死。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanzhen's nature is solely fierce and obstinate; his substance is fundamentally mediocre and foolish—a person of such petty stature deserves death ten thousand times over.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen is by nature fierce and obstinate, and by substance mediocre and foolish. A man of such petty stature deserves death ten thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 頃已寬其嚴典，念其微勞，屈法伸恩，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: Recently We already relaxed the severe statutes on his account, mindful of his slight merit, bending the law to extend grace and releasing him to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: We have already relaxed the full force of the law on his account, mindful of his slight service, bending the statutes to show mercy and sending him back to his estate.

sentences.zh: 仍乖克己，尚未知非；

translations.literal: Yet he still failed in self-restraint and has not yet recognized his fault;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still failed to restrain himself and has not yet recognized his fault;

sentences.zh: 既忘含煦之仁，別貯覬覦之望。

translations.literal: Having forgotten the benevolence of Our warm forbearance, he separately harbored ambitions of covetous desire.
translations.idiomatic: Having forgotten the warmth of Our forbearance, he secretly nursed ambitions of his own.

sentences.zh: 敢為嘯聚，仍欲動搖，不令之臣，共為睥睨；

translations.literal: He dared to gather and clamor, still wishing to stir unrest; unworthy ministers together cast sidelong glances;
translations.idiomatic: He dared to gather followers and stir trouble, still seeking to shake the throne; unworthy ministers together watched for their chance;

sentences.zh: 妄談休咎，仍懷怨望。

translations.literal: He recklessly spoke of fortune and calamity, still nursing resentment and discontent.
translations.idiomatic: He recklessly spoke of omens and disasters, still nursing resentment and discontent.

sentences.zh: 束兵裹甲，變服潛行，無顧君親，將圖不軌。

translations.literal: He bound up troops and wrapped armor, changed clothes and traveled secretly, heedless of sovereign and kin, intending to plot treason.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered armed men, changed clothes and traveled in secret, heedless of sovereign and kin, and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 按驗皆是，無所逃刑，首足異門，未雲塞責。

translations.literal: Investigation verified all of it; there is no escaping punishment. Beheading at separate gates would still not suffice to answer for the crime.
