translations.idiomatic: Investigation confirmed every charge; there is no escaping punishment. Even execution by beheading would scarcely answer for the crime.

sentences.zh: 朕猶不忘薄效，再舍罪人；

translations.literal: We still do not forget his slight service and again spare the criminal;
translations.idiomatic: We still do not forget his slight service and again spare the guilty man;

sentences.zh: 特寬斧鉞之誅，俾正投荒之典。

translations.literal: We especially waive the executioner's axe and cleaver, and instead apply the proper punishment of exile to the wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: We especially waive the death penalty and instead impose the proper punishment of exile to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 宜長流榛州百姓，委京兆府差綱遞送；

translations.literal: He should be exiled for life to Zhen Prefecture as a commoner; the metropolitan prefecture of Jingzhao is charged to assign escort couriers for delivery;
translations.idiomatic: He is to be exiled for life to Zhen Prefecture as a commoner, and the metropolitan prefecture of Jingzhao shall assign escort couriers to deliver him;

sentences.zh: 路次州縣，差人防援，至彼捉拘，勿許東西。

translations.literal: At counties and prefectures along the route, officials shall be assigned to guard and escort him; upon arrival there he shall be detained and not permitted to go east or west.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at every county and prefecture along the route shall guard and escort him; upon arrival he shall be detained and forbidden to travel east or west.

sentences.zh: 縱有非常之赦，不在會恩之限。

translations.literal: Even should there be an extraordinary amnesty, he shall not fall within the bounds of general mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Even should there be an extraordinary amnesty, he shall not be included within the bounds of general mercy.

sentences.zh: 凡百僚庶，宜體朕懷。

translations.literal: All officials and common subjects should embody Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Let all officials and subjects understand Our intent."

sentences.zh: =魚朝恩　=

translations.literal: = Yu Chaoen =
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chaoen

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩，天寶末以宦者入內侍省，初為品官，給事黃門。

translations.literal: Yu Chaoen, at the end of the Tianbao era entered the Palace Domestic Service as a eunuch; initially he was a ranked official serving at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chaoen entered the Palace Domestic Service as a eunuch near the end of the Tianbao era. At first he served as a ranked official at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 性黠惠，善宣答，通書計。

translations.literal: His nature was clever and quick; he was skilled at court announcements and responses, and versed in writing and reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever and quick-witted, skilled at delivering court announcements and responses, and versed in writing and accounts.

sentences.zh: 至德中，常令監軍事。

translations.literal: During the Zhide era he was often put in charge of supervising military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide era he was often assigned to supervise military affairs.

sentences.zh: 九節度討安慶緒於相州，不立統帥，以朝恩為觀軍容宣慰處置使。

translations.literal: When nine circuits' forces campaigned against An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture, no supreme commander was appointed; Chaoen was made Commissioner for Army Supervision, Comfort, and Disposition.
translations.idiomatic: When forces from nine circuits campaigned against An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture, no supreme commander was appointed, and Chaoen was made Commissioner for Army Supervision, Comfort, and Disposition.

sentences.zh: 觀軍容使名，自朝恩始也。

translations.literal: The title of army-supervision commissioner began with Chaoen.
translations.idiomatic: The title of army-supervision commissioner originated with Chaoen.

sentences.zh: 以功累加左監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was repeatedly promoted until he became Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was repeatedly promoted until he became Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 時郭子儀頻立大功，當代無出其右；

translations.literal: At that time Guo Ziyi repeatedly achieved great merit, and in the age none surpassed him;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guo Ziyi repeatedly won great victories, and no man of the age surpassed him;

sentences.zh: 朝恩妒其功高，屢行間諜；

translations.literal: Chaoen envied his towering achievements and repeatedly carried out covert intrigue;
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen envied his towering achievements and repeatedly sowed covert intrigue;

sentences.zh: 子儀悉心奉上，殊不介意。

translations.literal: Ziyi devoted himself wholeheartedly to serving the throne and took no notice at all.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi devoted himself wholeheartedly to serving the throne and paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 肅宗英悟，特察其心，故朝恩之間不行。

translations.literal: Suzong was perceptive and discerning, and specially perceived his heart, so Chaoen's intrigue did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was perceptive and saw through the matter, so Chaoen's intrigues did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 自相州之敗，史思明再陷河洛，朝恩常統禁軍鎮陜，以殿東夏。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Xiang Prefecture, when Shi Siming again took the He-Luo region, Chaoen regularly commanded the forbidden army garrisoning Shan, to guard the eastern heartland.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Xiang Prefecture, when Shi Siming again seized the He-Luo region, Chaoen regularly commanded the palace armies garrisoned at Shan to guard the eastern heartland.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，西蕃入犯京畿，代宗幸陜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, western barbarians invaded the capital region and Daizong fled to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangde, western tribes invaded the capital region and Emperor Daizong fled to Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時禁軍不集，征召離散，比至華陰，朝恩大軍遽至迎奉，六師方振。

translations.literal: At that time the forbidden army had not assembled; conscripts were scattered. When they reached Huayin, Chaoen's great army suddenly arrived to receive and escort them, and the six armies at last rallied.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the palace armies had not yet assembled and conscripts were scattered. By the time the court reached Huayin, Chaoen's main force suddenly arrived to receive the emperor, and the six armies at last rallied.

sentences.zh: 由是深加寵異，改為天下觀軍容宣慰處置使。

translations.literal: Because of this he received deep favor and special treatment, and his title was changed to Commissioner for Army Supervision, Comfort, and Disposition over All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he received extraordinary favor, and his title was changed to Commissioner for Army Supervision, Comfort, and Disposition over All Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 時四方未寧，萬務事殷，上方註意勛臣，朝恩專典神策軍，出入禁中，賞賜無算。

translations.literal: At that time the four quarters were not yet settled and myriad affairs pressed urgently; the emperor was concentrating attention on meritorious ministers while Chaoen exclusively managed the Shence Army, coming and going within the forbidden palace, with rewards and gifts beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was still unsettled and affairs pressed urgently on every side. While the emperor focused on meritorious ministers, Chaoen alone controlled the Shence Army, coming and going within the inner palace with rewards and gifts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 朝恩性本凡劣，恃勛自伐，靡所忌憚。

translations.literal: Chaoen's nature was fundamentally mediocre and base; relying on his merit he bragged of himself, fearing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen was by nature mediocre and base. Relying on his achievements, he vaunted himself and feared nothing.

sentences.zh: 時引腐儒及輕薄文士於門下，講授經籍，作為文章，粗能把筆釋義，乃大言於朝士之中，自謂有文武才幹，以邀恩寵。

translations.literal: At the time he drew in musty Confucians and frivolous literary men to his household, lecturing on the classics and composing writings; though he could roughly wield the brush and explain meaning, he then spoke boldly among court officials, claiming himself possessed of both civil and martial talent to court favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered pedantic Confucians and frivolous literati at his gate, lecturing on the classics and composing essays. Though he could barely wield a brush and explain a text, he spoke boldly among court officials, claiming both civil and martial talent in order to win favor.

sentences.zh: 上優遇之，加判國子監事，光祿、鴻臚、禮賓、內飛龍、閑廄等使。

translations.literal: The emperor treated him with exceptional favor, adding concurrent posts as Director of the Directorate of Education, and commissioner of the Offices of Imperial Entertainments, Ceremonial Reception, Ceremonial Guests, Inner Flying Dragon, and the Imperial Stud, among others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him with exceptional favor, adding concurrent posts as Director of the Directorate of Education and commissioner of the Offices of Imperial Entertainments, Ceremonial Reception, Ceremonial Guests, Inner Flying Dragon, and the Imperial Stud, among others.

sentences.zh: 赴國子監視事，特詔宰臣、百僚、六軍將軍送上，京兆府造食，教坊賜樂。

translations.literal: When he went to the Directorate of Education to attend to affairs, a special edict ordered chancellors, the hundred officials, and generals of the six armies to escort him there; the metropolitan prefecture prepared food, and the Music Office granted musical performers.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to the Directorate of Education to take up his duties, a special edict ordered chancellors, the hundred officials, and generals of the six armies to escort him. The metropolitan prefecture prepared food, and the Music Office supplied performers.

sentences.zh: 大臣群官二百餘人，皆以本官備章服充附學生，列於監之廊下，侍詔給錢萬貫充食本，以供學生廚料。

translations.literal: More than two hundred senior ministers and assembled officials all, in their official titles and complete ceremonial dress, served as attached students, arranged in ranks beneath the corridors of the directorate; imperial editors were granted ten thousand strings of cash as capital for provisions to supply the students' kitchen expenses.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred senior ministers and officials, wearing the full ceremonial dress of their ranks, served as attached students and lined up beneath the corridors of the directorate. The court granted ten thousand strings of cash as capital for provisions to supply the students' kitchen expenses.

sentences.zh: 朝恩恣橫，求取無厭，凡有奏請，以先允為度，幸臣未有其比。

translations.literal: Chaoen acted willfully and overbearingly, insatiable in his demands; whatever memorial he submitted had to be approved beforehand—among favored ministers none had his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen acted with unrestrained arrogance and insatiable greed. Every memorial he submitted had to be approved in advance. Among favored ministers, none had his equal.

sentences.zh: ，朝恩獻通化門外賜莊為寺，以資章敬太后冥福；

translations.literal: Chaoen offered the granted estate outside Tonghua Gate as a monastery, to accumulate posthumous merit for Empress Zhangjing;
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen offered the imperial estate granted him outside Tonghua Gate as a monastery to accumulate posthumous merit for Empress Zhangjing;

sentences.zh: 仍請以章敬為名，復加興造，窮極壯麗。

translations.literal: He further requested that it be named Zhangjing, and added new construction until it reached the utmost in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He further requested that it be named Zhangjing and undertook new construction until the monastery reached the utmost in splendor.

sentences.zh: 以城中材木不足充費，乃奏壞曲江亭館、華清宮觀樓及百司行廨、將相沒官宅給其用，土木之役，僅逾萬億。

translations.literal: Because timber within the city was insufficient to meet the expense, he memorialized to demolish pavilions and halls at Qujiang, towers at Huaqing Palace and its observatories, government bureau offices, and confiscated residences of generals and chancellors for materials; the earth-and-wood labor alone nearly exceeded ten billion.
translations.idiomatic: Because timber within the city could not meet the expense, he memorialized to demolish pavilions and halls at Qujiang, towers at Huaqing Palace, government offices, and confiscated residences of generals and chancellors for building materials. The construction costs alone ran to nearly ten billion cash.

sentences.zh: 三年，讓判國子監事，加韓國公。

translations.literal: In the third year he yielded the concurrent directorship of the Directorate of Education and was further enfeoffed as Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he relinquished his concurrent directorship of the Directorate of Education and was further enfeoffed as Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 章敬太后忌日，百僚於興唐寺行香，朝恩置齋饌於寺外之車坊，延宰臣百僚就食。

translations.literal: On the anniversary of Empress Zhangjing's death, the hundred officials performed incense rites at Xingtang Monastery; Chaoen set out a vegetarian feast in the carriage depot outside the monastery and invited chancellors and the hundred officials to dine.
translations.idiomatic: On the anniversary of Empress Zhangjing's death, the hundred officials performed incense rites at Xingtang Monastery. Chaoen set out a vegetarian feast in the carriage depot outside the monastery and invited chancellors and officials to dine.

sentences.zh: 朝恩恣口談時政，公卿惕息。

translations.literal: Chaoen freely lectured on current affairs; ministers and nobles held their breath in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen freely held forth on current affairs, and ministers and nobles held their breath in fear.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中相裏造、殿中侍御史李衎以正言折之。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Xiangli Zao of the Ministry of Revenue and Palace Censor Li Kan rebutted him with upright words.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangli Zao, a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, and Li Kan, a palace censor, rebutted him with forthright words.

sentences.zh: 朝恩不悅，乃罷會。

translations.literal: Chaoen was displeased and dissolved the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen was displeased and broke up the gathering.

sentences.zh: 後嘗釋奠於國子監。

translations.literal: Later he once performed the libation sacrifice at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Later he once performed the libation sacrifice at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 宰臣百僚皆會，朝恩講《易》，征《鼎卦》「覆餗」之義，以譏元載。

translations.literal: Chancellors and the hundred officials all assembled; Chaoen lectured on the Classic of Changes, citing the meaning of "overturned cauldron" from the Ding hexagram to mock Yuan Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors and the hundred officials all assembled. Chaoen lectured on the Classic of Changes, citing the Ding hexagram's image of the "overturned cauldron" to mock Yuan Zai.

sentences.zh: 載心銜之，陰圖除去之。

translations.literal: Zai nursed resentment in his heart and secretly plotted to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai nursed a grudge and secretly plotted to remove him.

sentences.zh: 上以朝恩太橫，亦惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor also hated him because Chaoen was too overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also hated Chaoen, finding him too overbearing.

sentences.zh: 載欲伺其便，巧中傷之；

translations.literal: Zai wished to watch for an opportunity and artfully strike him with injury;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai wished to watch for an opportunity and artfully destroy him;

sentences.zh: 乃用腹心崔昭為京兆尹，伺朝恩出處。

translations.literal: He therefore employed his intimate Cui Zhao as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao to watch Chaoen's comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore placed his trusted follower Cui Zhao in the post of metropolitan governor of Jingzhao to watch Chaoen's movements.

sentences.zh: 昭不吝財賂，潛與朝恩黨陜州觀察使皇甫溫相結，溫與昭協。

translations.literal: Cui Zhao did not stint in bribes and secretly connected with Huangfu Wen, the observer of Shan Prefecture, a member of Chaoen's faction; Wen and Zhao coordinated.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhao did not stint in bribes and secretly allied with Huangfu Wen, the observer of Shan Prefecture and a member of Chaoen's faction. Wen and Zhao worked in concert.

sentences.zh: 自是朝恩動靜，載皆知之，巨細悉以聞。

translations.literal: From this time Chaoen's every movement was known to Zai, and details great and small were all reported.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Yuan Zai knew Chaoen's every movement, and every detail was reported to him.

sentences.zh: 上益怒，朝恩未之察，日以驕橫。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier; Chaoen did not perceive it, becoming more arrogant by the day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier, but Chaoen did not perceive it and grew more arrogant by the day.

sentences.zh: 載奏加朝恩實封，又加皇甫溫權位，以肆其欲。

translations.literal: Zai memorialized to increase Chaoen's actual fief households and further raise Huangfu Wen's rank and position, to indulge their desires.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai memorialized to increase Chaoen's actual fief households and further elevate Huangfu Wen's rank and position, indulging their ambitions.

sentences.zh: 五年，朝恩所昵武將劉希暹微有過忤，上諷之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Chaoen's favored military officer Liu Xixian slightly overstepped in some offence; the emperor used indirect speech to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Chaoen's favored military officer Liu Xixian gave slight offence, and the emperor rebuked him indirectly.

sentences.zh: 詔罷朝恩觀軍容使，加實封通前一千戶。

translations.literal: An edict removed Chaoen as army-supervision commissioner and added to his actual fief, bringing the total to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Chaoen as army-supervision commissioner and increased his actual fief, bringing the total to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 朝恩始疑，然每朝謁，恩顧如常，亦不以載為意。

translations.literal: Chaoen began to suspect, yet each time he attended court audience the sovereign's gracious regard was as before, and he did not take Zai into account either.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen began to suspect trouble, yet at each court audience the emperor's gracious regard was unchanged, and he paid Yuan Zai no heed.

sentences.zh: 會寒食宴近臣，朝恩入謁。

translations.literal: On the occasion of the Cold Food festival banquet for close ministers, Chaoen entered for audience.
translations.idiomatic: At a Cold Food festival banquet for close ministers, Chaoen entered for audience.

sentences.zh: 先是，每宴罷，必出還營，是日有詔留之。

translations.literal: Previously, whenever the banquet ended he always left to return to camp; this day there was an edict detaining him.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, whenever the banquet ended he always left to return to camp, but this day an edict detained him.

sentences.zh: 朝恩始懼，言頗悖慢，上亦以舊恩不之責。

translations.literal: Chaoen began to fear; his words were quite rebellious and insolent, but the emperor, owing to old favor, did not rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen began to fear for his life. His words turned quite insolent, but the emperor, remembering past service, did not rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 是日朝恩還第，自經而卒。

translations.literal: That day Chaoen returned to his residence and died by hanging himself.
translations.idiomatic: That day Chaoen returned to his residence and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 劉希暹亦下獄賜死。

translations.literal: Liu Xixian was also thrown into prison and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xixian was also thrown into prison and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 希暹，出自戎伍，有膂力，形貌光偉，以騎射聞。

translations.literal: Xixian came from the military ranks; he had strength in his limbs, a bright and imposing appearance, and was known for horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian came from the military ranks. He was powerfully built, bright and imposing in appearance, and renowned for horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 朝恩用之為神策都虞候，封交河郡王。

translations.literal: Chaoen employed him as chief adjutant of the Shence Army and enfeoffed him as Prince of Jiaohe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen appointed him chief adjutant of the Shence Army and enfeoffed him as Prince of Jiaohe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 善候朝恩意旨，深被委信。

translations.literal: He was adept at reading Chaoen's intentions and was deeply entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: He was adept at reading Chaoen's intentions and enjoyed his deep trust.

sentences.zh: 累遷至太僕卿，與兵馬使王駕鶴同掌禁兵，所為不法。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly until he became Minister of the Stud; together with army-horse commissioner Wang Jiahe he jointly controlled the forbidden army, and their conduct was unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly until he became Minister of the Stud. Together with army-horse commissioner Wang Jiahe he jointly controlled the palace armies, and their conduct was unlawful.

sentences.zh: 諷朝恩於北軍置獄，召坊市兇惡少年，羅織城內富人，誣以違法，捕置獄中，忍酷考訊，錄其家產，並沒於軍。

translations.literal: He persuaded Chaoen to establish a prison in the northern army camp, summon vicious youths from the wards and markets, frame wealthy men within the city on charges of violation, seize and imprison them, torture them with cruel examinations, record their family property, and confiscate it all to the army.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded Chaoen to establish a prison in the northern army camp and summon vicious youths from the wards and markets. They framed wealthy men in the city on charges of wrongdoing, seized and imprisoned them, tortured them cruelly, inventoried their property, and confiscated it all for the army.

sentences.zh: 或有舉選之士，財貨稍殷，客於旅舍，遇橫死者非一。

translations.literal: Some candidates for office, whose wealth was somewhat ample and who lodged at inns, met violent death in more than one case.
translations.idiomatic: Some examination candidates of modest wealth who lodged at inns met violent deaths in more than one case.

sentences.zh: 坊市苦之，謂之「入地牢」。

translations.literal: The wards and markets suffered bitterly from this and called it "entering the underground dungeon."
translations.idiomatic: The wards and markets suffered bitterly from this and called it "being sent to the underground dungeon."

sentences.zh: 捕賊吏有賈明觀者，尤兇蠹，以屢置大獄，家產巨萬。

translations.literal: Among the thief-catching clerks there was one Jia Mingguan, especially vicious and corrupt; through repeatedly setting up major cases, his household property reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Among the thief-catching clerks was one Jia Mingguan, especially vicious and corrupt. Through repeatedly fabricating major cases, he amassed household property in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 希暹黨之，地在禁密，人無敢言者。

translations.literal: Xixian patronized him; the ground was within the forbidden and secret precinct, and no one dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian protected him. The prison lay within the forbidden inner precinct, and no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 朝恩死，上寬宥之。

translations.literal: Chaoen died; the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaoen's death, the emperor showed him leniency.

sentences.zh: 以素志非順，慮不見容，常自疑懼。

translations.literal: Because his long-standing disposition was not compliant, he feared he would not be tolerated and constantly doubted and feared.
translations.idiomatic: Because his disposition had long been insubordinate, he feared he would not be tolerated and lived in constant suspicion and dread.

sentences.zh: 與王駕鶴聯職，希暹辭多不遜。

translations.literal: He shared office with Wang Jiahe, and Xixian's words were often not deferential.
translations.idiomatic: He held joint office with Wang Jiahe, and Xixian's speech was often insolent.

sentences.zh: 駕鶴純謹，上信任之，至是以希暹語上聞，乃誅之。

translations.literal: Jiahe was pure and careful; the emperor trusted him. At this time Xixian's words reached the emperor's ears, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiahe was upright and conscientious, and the emperor trusted him. On this occasion Xixian's words reached the emperor, and Xixian was put to death.

sentences.zh: 賈明觀者，本萬年縣捕賊吏。

translations.literal: Jia Mingguan was originally a thief-catching clerk of Wannian County.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mingguan had originally been a thief-catching clerk in Wannian County.

sentences.zh: 事希暹，恣為兇惡，毒甚豺狼。

translations.literal: He served Xixian, indulged in violence and wickedness, and was more vicious than wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Xixian, he indulged in violence and cruelty, savage as a wolf.

sentences.zh: 朝恩、希暹既死，元載復受明觀奸謀，潛容之，特奏令江西效力。

translations.literal: After Chaoen and Xixian had died, Yuan Zai again accepted Mingguan's treacherous schemes, secretly sheltered him, and specially memorialized that he be sent to serve in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaoen and Xixian were dead, Yuan Zai again took Mingguan's treacherous counsel, sheltered him in secret, and specially memorialized to send him to serve in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明觀將出城，百姓數萬人懷磚石候之，載令市吏止約。

translations.literal: When Mingguan was about to leave the city, tens of thousands of common people waited for him with bricks and stones in their arms; Zai ordered market clerks to restrain and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingguan was about to leave the city, tens of thousands of commoners waited for him with bricks and stones in hand. Yuan Zai ordered market officials to restrain and calm the crowd.

sentences.zh: 明觀在洪州二年，觀察使魏少遊容之。

translations.literal: Mingguan was in Hong Prefecture for two years, and the observer Wei Shaoyou sheltered him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingguan spent two years in Hong Prefecture, where the observer Wei Shaoyou sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 及路嗣恭代少遊，至郡之日，召明觀笞殺之。

translations.literal: When Lu Sigong replaced Shaoyou, on the day he reached the prefecture he summoned Mingguan and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Sigong replaced Shaoyou, on the day he arrived at the prefecture he summoned Mingguan and had him flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 識者減魏之名，多路之正。

translations.literal: Those who understood the matter lowered Wei's reputation and praised Lu's rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment lowered Wei's reputation and praised Lu's righteousness.

sentences.zh: 朝恩素待禮部尚書裴士淹，戶部侍郎、判度支第五琦，二人亦坐貶官。

translations.literal: Chaoen had always treated well the Minister of Rites Pei Shiyan and the Vice Minister of Revenue and acting commissioner of the Finance Bureau Diwu Qi; both men were also implicated and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen had long favored the Minister of Rites Pei Shiyan and the Vice Minister of Revenue and acting commissioner of the Finance Bureau, Diwu Qi. Both men were also implicated and demoted.

sentences.zh: =竇文場、霍仙鳴=

translations.literal: = Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming =
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming

sentences.zh: 竇文場、霍仙鳴者，始在東宮事德宗。

translations.literal: Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming had at first served Dezong in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming had originally served Dezong in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 初魚朝恩誅後，內官不復典兵，德宗以親軍委白志貞。

translations.literal: At first, after Yu Chaoen was executed, inner officials no longer commanded troops; Dezong entrusted the imperial guard to Bai Zhiben.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Chaoen was executed, inner officials no longer commanded troops, and Dezong entrusted the imperial guard to Bai Zhiben.

sentences.zh: 志貞多納豪民賂，補為軍士，取其傭直，身無在軍者，但以名籍請給而已。

translations.literal: Zhiben frequently accepted bribes from powerful commoners, enrolled them as soldiers, and took their pay; none were actually in the army—they merely used their names on the rolls to claim rations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiben frequently accepted bribes from wealthy commoners, enrolled them as soldiers, and pocketed their pay. None actually served in the army; they existed only on the rolls to claim rations.

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，帝召禁軍禦賊，志貞召集無素，是時並無至者，唯文場、仙鳴率諸宦者及親王左右從行。

translations.literal: During the Jingshi mutiny, the emperor summoned the forbidden army to repel the rebels. Zhiben mustered them without order; at that time none arrived. Only Wenchang and Xianming led the various eunuchs and the attendants of imperial princes to follow on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingshi mutiny, the emperor summoned the palace armies to repel the rebels. Zhiben mustered them without discipline, and none arrived. Only Wenchang and Xianming led the eunuchs and the attendants of imperial princes in following the emperor.

sentences.zh: 志貞貶官，左右禁旅，悉委文場主之。

translations.literal: Zhiben was demoted; the left and right forbidden guards were all entrusted to Wenchang to command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiben was demoted, and command of the left and right palace guards was entirely entrusted to Wenchang.

sentences.zh: 從幸山南，兩軍漸集。

translations.literal: Following the emperor's journey to Shannan, the two armies gradually assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor into exile in Shannan, the two armies gradually assembled.

sentences.zh: 德宗還京，頗忌宿將，凡握兵多者，悉罷之。

translations.literal: When Dezong returned to the capital, he greatly feared veteran generals; all who held substantial military power were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned to the capital, he deeply distrusted veteran generals and dismissed all who held substantial military power.

sentences.zh: 禁旅文場、仙鳴分統焉。

translations.literal: The forbidden guard was divided between Wenchang and Xianming to command.
translations.idiomatic: Command of the palace guard was divided between Wenchang and Xianming.

sentences.zh: 六月，特立護軍中尉兩員、中護軍兩員，以帥禁軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, two Protector Army Commandants and two Central Protector Generals were specially established to command the forbidden army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, two Protector Army Commandants and two Central Protector Generals were specially established to command the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 乃以文場為左神策護軍中尉，仙鳴為右神策護軍中尉，右神威軍使張尚進為右神策中護軍，內謁者監焦希望為左神策中護軍，自文場等始也。

translations.literal: Then Wenchang was made Left Shence Protector Army Commandant, Xianming Right Shence Protector Army Commandant, Zhang Shangjin, commissioner of the Right Shenwei Army, Right Shence Central Protector General, and Jiao Xiwang, Director of Palace Reception, Left Shence Central Protector General. This began with Wenchang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang was appointed Left Shence Protector Army Commandant, Xianming Right Shence Protector Army Commandant, Zhang Shangjin, commissioner of the Right Shenwei Army, Right Shence Central Protector General, and Jiao Xiwang, Director of Palace Reception, Left Shence Central Protector General. This practice began with Wenchang and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 時竇、霍之權，振於天下，籓鎮節將，多出禁軍，臺省清要，時出其門。

translations.literal: At that time the power of Dou and Huo shook the realm; frontier military commissioners mostly came from the forbidden army, and prestigious posts in the Secretariat and ministries often issued from their gate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the power of Dou and Huo shook the realm. Frontier military commissioners mostly came from the palace armies, and prestigious posts in the Secretariat and ministries often issued from their faction.

sentences.zh: 文場累加驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Wenchang was repeatedly promoted to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang was repeatedly promoted until he reached General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 是歲仙鳴病，帝賜馬十匹，令於諸寺為僧齋以祈福。

translations.literal: That year Xianming fell ill; the emperor bestowed ten horses and ordered vegetarian feasts for monks at various temples to pray for blessings.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xianming fell ill. The emperor bestowed ten horses and ordered vegetarian feasts for monks at various temples to pray for his recovery.

sentences.zh: 久病不愈，十四年，倉卒而卒。

translations.literal: His long illness did not heal; in the fourteenth year he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: His long illness did not improve, and in the fourteenth year he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 上疑左右小使正將食中加毒，配流者數十人。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected that attendants and petty officers had put poison in his food; several dozen were sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected that attendants and petty officers had poisoned his food, and several dozen were sentenced to exile.

sentences.zh: 仙鳴死後，以開府內常侍第五守亮為右軍中尉。

translations.literal: After Xianming's death, Diwu Shouliang, Palace Attendant with the status of Grand Preceptor, was made Right Army Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianming's death, Diwu Shouliang, Palace Attendant with the status of Grand Preceptor, was appointed Right Army Commandant.

sentences.zh: 文場連表請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: Wenchang repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 十五年已後，楊志廉、孫榮義為左右軍中尉，亦踵竇、霍之事，怙寵驕恣。

translations.literal: After the fifteenth year, Yang Zhilian and Sun Rongyi served as Left and Right Army Commandants; they also followed the example of Dou and Huo, relying on favor and growing arrogant and willful.
translations.idiomatic: After the fifteenth year, Yang Zhilian and Sun Rongyi served as Left and Right Army Commandants. They followed the example of Dou and Huo, relying on imperial favor and growing arrogant and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 貪利冒寵之徒，利其納賄，多附麗之。

translations.literal: Men greedy for profit and eager for favor, profiting from their acceptance of bribes, mostly attached themselves to them.
translations.idiomatic: Men greedy for profit and eager for favor, drawn by their readiness to accept bribes, flocked to attach themselves to them.

sentences.zh: 至於貞元末，宦官復盛。

translations.literal: By the end of the Zhenyuan era, eunuchs flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Zhenyuan era, eunuch power had revived.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，王叔文用事，與韋執誼謀奪神策軍權，乃用宿將範希朝為京西北禁軍都將。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne, Wang Shuwen held power; together with Wei Zhiyi he plotted to seize control of the Shence Army and therefore appointed the veteran general Fan Xichao as chief commander of the forbidden armies northwest of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended the throne, Wang Shuwen held power. Together with Wei Zhiyi he plotted to seize control of the Shence Army and appointed the veteran general Fan Xichao chief commander of the palace armies northwest of the capital.

sentences.zh: 事未行，為內官俱文珍等所排，叔文貶而止。

translations.literal: Before the plan could be carried out, it was blocked by the inner officials Ju Wenzhen and others; Shuwen was demoted and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan could be carried out, the inner officials Ju Wenzhen and others blocked it. Shuwen was demoted, and the scheme came to nothing.

sentences.zh: =俱文珍=

translations.literal: = Ju Wenzhen =
translations.idiomatic: Ju Wenzhen

sentences.zh: 俱文珍，貞元末宦官，後從義父姓，曰劉貞亮。

translations.literal: Ju Wenzhen was a eunuch of the late Zhenyuan era; later he took his adoptive father's surname and was called Liu Zhenliang.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Wenzhen was a eunuch of the late Zhenyuan era. Later he took his adoptive father's surname and was known as Liu Zhenliang.

sentences.zh: 性忠正，剛而蹈義。

translations.literal: His nature was loyal and upright, firm and devoted to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was loyal and upright by nature, resolute and devoted to righteousness.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，風疾不能視朝政，而宦官李忠言與牛美人侍病。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne, a wind ailment prevented him from attending to court affairs, and the eunuch Li Zhongyan and the Lady Niu attended him in his illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended the throne, a paralytic ailment kept him from attending to court affairs, and the eunuch Li Zhongyan and the Lady Niu attended him in his illness.

sentences.zh: 美人受旨於帝，復宣之於忠言；

translations.literal: The Lady received the emperor's instructions and then proclaimed them to Zhongyan;
translations.idiomatic: The Lady received the emperor's instructions and then relayed them to Zhongyan;

sentences.zh: 忠言授之王叔文。

translations.literal: Zhongyan transmitted them to Wang Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan passed them on to Wang Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 叔文與朝士柳宗元、劉禹錫、韓日華圖議，然後下中書，俾韋執誼施行，故王之權振天下。

translations.literal: Shuwen deliberated with court gentlemen Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, and Han Rihua, then sent matters down to the Secretariat and had Wei Zhiyi carry them out; therefore Wang's power shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen deliberated with court gentlemen Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, and Han Rihua, then sent matters down to the Secretariat for Wei Zhiyi to execute. Thus Wang's power shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 叔文欲奪宦者兵權，每忠言宣命，內臣無敢言者，唯貞亮建議與之爭。

translations.literal: Shuwen wished to seize military power from the eunuchs; whenever Zhongyan proclaimed an edict, none of the inner officials dared speak—only Zhenliang offered counsel and disputed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen sought to seize military power from the eunuchs. Whenever Zhongyan proclaimed an edict, none of the inner officials dared object—only Zhenliang offered counsel and disputed with him.

sentences.zh: 知其朋徒熾，慮隳朝政，乃與中官劉光琦、薛文珍、尚衍、解玉等謀，奏請立廣陵王為皇太子，勾當軍國大事。

translations.literal: Knowing that his faction was growing strong and fearing the ruin of court governance, he plotted with the inner officials Liu Guangqi, Xue Wenzhen, Shang Yan, Jie Yu, and others, memorializing to install the Prince of Guangling as crown prince to manage state and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Shuwen's faction was growing strong and fearing the ruin of court governance, he plotted with the inner officials Liu Guangqi, Xue Wenzhen, Shang Yan, Jie Yu, and others. They memorialized to install the Prince of Guangling as crown prince and entrust him with state and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 順宗可之。

translations.literal: Shunzong approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 貞亮遂召學士衛次公、鄭絪、李程、王涯入金鑾殿，草立儲君詔。

translations.literal: Zhenliang then summoned the academicians Wei Cigong, Zheng Yin, Li Cheng, and Wang Ya into the Hall of Golden Bells to draft the edict installing the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenliang then summoned the academicians Wei Cigong, Zheng Yin, Li Cheng, and Wang Ya into the Hall of Golden Bells to draft the edict installing the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 及太子受內禪，盡逐叔文之黨，政事悉委舊臣，時議嘉貞亮之忠藎。

translations.literal: When the crown prince received the inner abdication, he entirely expelled Shuwen's faction and entrusted all government affairs to former ministers; contemporary opinion praised Zhenliang's loyal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince received the inner abdication, he expelled Shuwen's entire faction and entrusted government affairs to the former ministers. Contemporary opinion praised Zhenliang's loyal devotion.

sentences.zh: 累遷至右衛大將軍，知內侍省事。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly until he became General of the Right Guard and Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly until he became General of the Right Guard and Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 卒，憲宗思其翊戴之功，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When he died, Xianzong remembered his service in supporting the enthronement and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor with the Protocol of Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Xianzong remembered how he had helped secure the succession and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor with the Protocol of Three Offices.

sentences.zh: =吐突承璀=

translations.literal: = Tu Tu Chenghui =
translations.idiomatic: Tu Tu Chenghui

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀，幼以小黃門直東宮，性敏慧，有才幹。

translations.literal: Tu Tu Chenghui, in youth as a junior palace attendant served in the Eastern Palace; his nature was keen and clever, and he had talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Tu Chenghui had served in the Eastern Palace as a junior palace attendant from youth. He was keen and clever by nature, with talent and ability.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，授內常侍，知內省事，左監門將軍。

translations.literal: When Xianzong ascended the throne, he was appointed Palace Attendant, Director of Palace Affairs, and General of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong ascended the throne, Chenghui was appointed Palace Attendant, Director of Palace Affairs, and General of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 俄授左軍中尉、功德使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Army Commandant and Commissioner of Meritorious Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Left Army Commandant and Commissioner of Meritorious Works.

sentences.zh: 四年，王承宗叛，詔以承璀為河中、河南、浙西、宣歙等道赴鎮州行營兵馬招討等使，內侍省常侍宋惟澄為河南、陜州、河陽已來館驛使，內官曹淮玉、劉國珍、馬江朝等分為河北行營糧料館驛等使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wang Chengzong rebelled. An edict appointed Chenghui Commissioner for Recruiting and Punitive Operations and other duties for the field headquarters marching on Zhen Prefecture across the circuits of Hezhong, Henan, Zhexi, and Xuanshe; Song Weicheng, Palace Attendant of the Palace Domestic Service, was made Commissioner of Post Stations from Henan and Shan Prefectures and Heyang onward; and the inner officials Cao Huaiyu, Liu Guozhen, Ma Jiangchao, and others were respectively made commissioners of grain supplies and post stations for the Hebei field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wang Chengzong rebelled. An edict appointed Chenghui Commissioner for Recruiting and Punitive Operations for the field headquarters marching on Zhen Prefecture across the circuits of Hezhong, Henan, Zhexi, and Xuanshe. Song Weicheng, Palace Attendant of the Palace Domestic Service, was made Commissioner of Post Stations from Henan and Shan Prefectures and Heyang onward, and the inner officials Cao Huaiyu, Liu Guozhen, Ma Jiangchao, and others were appointed commissioners of grain supplies and post stations for the Hebei field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 諫官、御史上疏相屬，皆言自古無中貴人為兵馬統帥者，補闕獨孤郁、段平仲尤激切。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials and censorial officials submitted memorials one after another, all saying that since antiquity no honored inner official had served as commander of troops; the remonstrance clerk Dugu Yu and Duan Pingzhong were especially forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials and censorial officials submitted memorial after memorial, all declaring that since antiquity no honored inner official had commanded troops. The remonstrance clerk Dugu Yu and Duan Pingzhong were especially forceful.

sentences.zh: 憲宗不獲已，改為充鎮州已來招撫處置等使。

translations.literal: Xianzong, having no alternative, changed the appointment to Commissioner for Pacification and Disposition from Zhen Prefecture onward.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, left with no alternative, changed the appointment to Commissioner for Pacification and Disposition from Zhen Prefecture onward.

sentences.zh: 及承璀率禁軍上路，帝御通化門樓，慰諭遣之。

translations.literal: When Chenghui led the forbidden army onto the road, the emperor mounted the gate tower at Tonghua Gate to comfort and instruct them as he sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenghui led the palace armies onto the road, the emperor mounted the gate tower at Tonghua Gate to comfort and instruct them as he sent them off.

sentences.zh: 出師經年無功，乃遣密人告王承宗，令上疏待罪，許以罷兵為解。

translations.literal: The campaign went out for a year without success; he then sent a secret agent to tell Wang Chengzong to submit a memorial awaiting punishment, promising withdrawal of troops as the terms of settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign dragged on for a year without success. Chenghui then sent a secret agent to tell Wang Chengzong to submit a memorial awaiting punishment, promising withdrawal of troops as the terms of settlement.

sentences.zh: 仍奏昭義節度使盧從史素與賊通，許為承宗求節鉞。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Lu Congshi, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, had long been in communication with the rebels and had promised to seek a commissioner's seal for Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that Lu Congshi, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, had long colluded with the rebels and had promised to seek a commissioner's seal for Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 乃誘潞州牙將烏重胤謀執從史送京師。

translations.literal: He then induced Wu Chongyin, a garrison officer of Lu Prefecture, to plot the seizure of Congshi and his delivery to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then induced Wu Chongyin, a garrison officer at Lu Prefecture, to plot Congshi's capture and delivery to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及承宗表至，朝廷議罷兵，承璀班師，仍為禁軍中尉。

translations.literal: When Chengzong's memorial arrived, the court deliberated on withdrawing troops; Chenghui withdrew the army and remained Commandant of the forbidden army.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong's memorial arrived, the court deliberated on withdrawing troops. Chenghui withdrew the army and remained Commandant of the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 段平仲抗疏極論承璀輕謀弊賦，請斬之以謝天下，憲宗不獲已，降為軍器使。

translations.literal: Duan Pingzhong submitted a forceful memorial vehemently arguing that Chenghui's rash schemes had harmed taxation and requesting his execution to appease the realm; Xianzong, having no alternative, demoted him to Commissioner of Military Equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pingzhong submitted a forceful memorial vehemently arguing that Chenghui's rash schemes had harmed taxation and requesting his execution to appease the realm. Xianzong, having no alternative, demoted Chenghui to Commissioner of Military Equipment.

sentences.zh: 俄復為左衛上將軍，知內侍省事。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Senior General of the Left Guard and Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again appointed Senior General of the Left Guard and Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 時弓箭庫使劉希先取羽林大將軍孫璹錢二十萬，以求方鎮，事發賜死，辭相告訐，事連承璀，乃出為淮南節度監軍使。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Xixian, commissioner of the Bow and Arrow Storehouse, took two hundred thousand in cash from Sun Zan, General of the Forest of Feathers, to seek a frontier commission; when the affair was exposed he was granted death, and in his testimony he implicated one another; the matter connected to Chenghui, who was then sent out as army supervisor of the Huainan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Xixian, commissioner of the Bow and Arrow Storehouse, took two hundred thousand in cash from Sun Zan, General of the Forest of Feathers, in exchange for a frontier commission. When the affair was exposed he was ordered to take his own life, and in his testimony he implicated others. The matter touched Chenghui, who was then sent out as army supervisor of the Huainan military commission.

sentences.zh: 太子通事舍人李涉，性狂險，投匭上書，論希先、承璀無罪，不宜貶戮。

translations.literal: Li She, Master of Ceremonies Attendant of the Crown Prince, was by nature reckless and dangerous; he submitted a letter through the complaint box arguing that Xixian and Chenghui were innocent and should not be demoted or executed.
translations.idiomatic: Li She, Master of Ceremonies Attendant of the Crown Prince, was reckless and dangerous by nature. He submitted a letter through the complaint box arguing that Xixian and Chenghui were innocent and should not be demoted or executed.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫、知匭事孔戣，見涉疏之副本，不受其章。

translations.literal: Kong Kui, Remonstrance Grandee and Commissioner of the Complaint Box, saw a copy of She's memorial and refused to accept his petition.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Kui, Remonstrance Grandee and commissioner of the complaint box, saw a copy of She's memorial and refused to accept his petition.

sentences.zh: 涉持疏於光順門欲進之，戣上疏論其纖邪，貶涉硤州司倉。

translations.literal: She carried the memorial to Guangshun Gate intending to submit it; Kui memorialized arguing his subtle wickedness, and She was demoted to Warehouse Clerk of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: She carried the memorial to Guangshun Gate intending to submit it. Kong Kui memorialized denouncing his subtle wickedness, and She was demoted to Warehouse Clerk of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上待承璀之意未已，而宰相李絳在翰林，時數論承璀之過，故出之。

translations.literal: The emperor's favor toward Chenghui had not yet ended, but the chief minister Li Jiang was in the Hanlin Academy and frequently discussed Chenghui's faults; therefore Chenghui was sent out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favor toward Chenghui had not yet ended, but Chief Minister Li Jiang was in the Hanlin Academy and frequently criticized Chenghui's faults. For this reason Chenghui was sent out.

sentences.zh: 八年，欲召承璀還，乃罷絳相位。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, wishing to recall Chenghui, he dismissed Jiang from the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, wishing to recall Chenghui, the emperor dismissed Li Jiang from the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 承璀還，復為神策中尉。

translations.literal: Chenghui returned and again became Shence Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui returned and was again appointed Shence Commandant.

sentences.zh: 惠昭太子薨，承璀建議請立澧王寬為太子，憲宗不納，立遂王宥。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Huizhao died, Chenghui memorialized requesting that Prince Li Kuan be installed as crown prince; Xianzong did not accept it and installed Prince Sui You instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Huizhao died, Chenghui memorialized to install Prince Li Kuan as crown prince. Xianzong did not accept the proposal and installed Prince Sui You instead.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，銜承璀不佑己，誅之。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, he resented Chenghui for not supporting him and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended the throne, he resented Chenghui for not supporting him and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 敬宗時，中尉馬存亮論承璀之冤，詔雪之，仍令假子士曄以禮收葬。

translations.literal: During Jingzong's reign, Commandant Ma Cunliang argued Chenghui's injustice; an edict cleared his name and ordered his adopted son Shi Ye to bury him with proper rites.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingzong's reign, Commandant Ma Cunliang argued that Chenghui had been wronged. An edict cleared his name and ordered his adopted son Shi Ye to bury him with proper rites.

sentences.zh: =王守澄=

translations.literal: = Wang Shoucheng =
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng

sentences.zh: 王守澄，元和末宦者。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng was a eunuch of the late Yuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng was a eunuch of the late Yuanhe era.

sentences.zh: 憲宗疾大漸，內官陳弘慶等弒逆。

translations.literal: When Xianzong's illness grew grave, the inner officials Chen Hongqing and others committed regicide.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong's illness grew grave, the inner officials Chen Hongqing and others murdered him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗英武，威德在人，內官秘之，不敢除討，但云藥發暴崩。

translations.literal: Xianzong was heroic and martial, and his authority and virtue lived in men's hearts; the inner officials kept it secret and dared not pursue and punish the culprits, saying only that medicine took effect and he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong had been heroic and martial, and his authority and virtue still lived in men's hearts. The inner officials kept the truth secret and dared not pursue the culprits, saying only that medicine took effect and he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 時守澄與中尉馬進潭、梁守謙、劉承偕、韋元素等定冊立穆宗皇帝。

translations.literal: At that time Shoucheng, together with Commandants Ma Jintan, Liang Shouqian, Liu Chengjie, Wei Yuansu, and others, settled the enthronement of Emperor Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shoucheng, together with Commandants Ma Jintan, Liang Shouqian, Liu Chengjie, Wei Yuansu, and others, settled the enthronement of Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，守澄知樞密事。

translations.literal: During the Changqing era, Shoucheng managed secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing era, Shoucheng took charge of confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，元和中，守澄為徐州監軍，遇翼城醫人鄭註，出入節度使李醖家。

translations.literal: At first, during the Yuanhe era, Shoucheng was army supervisor of Xuzhou and encountered the physician Zheng Zhu of Yicheng, who came and went in the household of the military commissioner Li Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yuanhe era, Shoucheng was army supervisor of Xuzhou and encountered the physician Zheng Zhu of Yicheng, who frequented the household of the military commissioner Li Yun.

sentences.zh: 註敏悟過人，博通典藝，棋奕醫卜，尤臻於妙，人見之者，無不歡然。

translations.literal: Zhu was keen and perceptive beyond others, broadly versed in classical arts; in chess, medicine, and divination he especially reached mastery, and all who saw him were delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was keen and perceptive beyond ordinary men, broadly versed in classical arts. In chess, medicine, and divination he especially reached mastery, and all who met him were delighted.

sentences.zh: 註嘗為李醖煮黃金，服一刀圭，可愈痿弱重膇之疾，復能反老成童。

translations.literal: Zhu once prepared gold for Li Yun to consume; one small spoonful could cure ailments of weakness and swollen legs, and could even reverse age and restore youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu once prepared gold for Li Yun to consume. One small spoonful, he claimed, could cure ailments of weakness and swollen legs and even reverse age and restore youth.

sentences.zh: 醖與守澄服之，頗效。

translations.literal: Yun and Shoucheng took it and it was quite effective.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun and Shoucheng took it, and it proved quite effective.

sentences.zh: 守澄知樞密，薦引入禁中，穆宗待之亦厚。

translations.literal: When Shoucheng managed secretariat affairs, he recommended Zhu for entry into the inner palace, and Muzong also treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shoucheng took charge of confidential state affairs, he recommended Zhu for entry into the inner palace, and Muzong treated him generously as well.

sentences.zh: 註多奇詭，每與守澄言必通夕。

translations.literal: Zhu was full of strange and devious notions; whenever he spoke with Shoucheng they talked through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was full of strange and devious notions, and whenever he spoke with Shoucheng they talked through the night.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，守澄為驃騎大將軍，充右軍中尉。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Shoucheng was made General of Agile Cavalry and served as Right Army Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Shoucheng was made General of Agile Cavalry and appointed Right Army Commandant.

sentences.zh: 註復得幸於文宗，後依倚守澄，大為奸弊。

translations.literal: Zhu again gained favor with Wenzong; later relying on Shoucheng, he committed great wickedness and corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu again gained favor with Wenzong. Later, relying on Shoucheng, he committed great wickedness and corruption.

sentences.zh: 文宗以元和逆黨尚在，其黨大盛，心常憤惋，端居不怡。

translations.literal: Wenzong, because the Yuanhe faction of regicides still survived and their party had grown great, was constantly indignant and resentful in heart and sat at ease without joy.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Yuanhe faction of regicides still survived and their party had grown powerful, Wenzong was constantly indignant and sat brooding in discontent.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士宋申錫嘗獨對探知，上略言其意，申錫請漸除其逼。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academician Song Shenxi once in a private audience probed and learned the emperor's mind; the emperor briefly stated his intent, and Shenxi requested gradually removing their pressure.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Academician Song Shenxi once probed the emperor's mind in a private audience. The emperor briefly stated his intent, and Shenxi offered to remove the eunuchs' pressure gradually.

sentences.zh: 帝亦以申錫沈厚有方略，為其事可成，乃用為宰相。

translations.literal: The emperor also considered Shenxi deep, steady, and strategic, and believed the affair could succeed; he therefore appointed him chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also considered Shenxi deep, steady, and strategic, and believed the affair could succeed. He therefore appointed him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 申錫謀未果，為註所察，守澄乃令軍吏豆盧著誣告申錫與漳王謀逆，申錫坐貶。

translations.literal: Shenxi's plot did not succeed and was detected by Zhu; Shoucheng then had the army clerk Dou Luzhe falsely accuse Shenxi of plotting rebellion with the Prince of Zhang, and Shenxi was implicated and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi's plot did not succeed and was detected by Zhu. Shoucheng then had the army clerk Dou Luzhe falsely accuse Shenxi of plotting rebellion with the Prince of Zhang, and Shenxi was implicated and demoted.

sentences.zh: 宰相李逢吉從子訓，與註交通，訓亦機詭萬端，二人情義相得，俱為守澄所重。

translations.literal: Li Xun, nephew of Chief Minister Li Fengji, was in contact with Zhu; Xun was also endlessly crafty and cunning, and the two were bound in mutual affection and both highly valued by Shoucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, nephew of Chief Minister Li Fengji, was in contact with Zhu. Xun was also endlessly crafty and cunning, and the two were bound in mutual affection and both highly valued by Shoucheng.

sentences.zh: 復引訓入禁中，為上講《周易》。

translations.literal: He again introduced Xun into the inner palace to lecture the emperor on the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He again introduced Xun into the inner palace to lecture the emperor on the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 既得幸，又探知帝旨，復以除宦官謀中帝意。

translations.literal: Once he had gained favor, he again probed the emperor's intent and, with a plan to remove the eunuchs, struck the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had gained favor, he again probed the emperor's intent and, with a plan to remove the eunuchs, struck exactly what the emperor wished.

sentences.zh: 帝以訓才辯縱橫，以為其事必捷，待以殊寵，自流人中用為學官，充侍進學士。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Xun's talent for eloquent and sweeping argument, believed the affair would surely succeed and treated him with exceptional favor, appointing him from among the exiled to be a learning official and Attendant Academician-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, impressed by Xun's talent for eloquent and sweeping argument, believed the affair would surely succeed and treated him with exceptional favor, appointing him from among the exiled to be a learning official and Attendant Academician-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 時仇士良有翌上之功，為守澄所抑，位未通顯。

translations.literal: At that time Qiu Shiliang had merit in supporting the enthronement but was suppressed by Shoucheng, and his rank had not yet reached prominence.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qiu Shiliang had helped secure the enthronement, but Shoucheng kept him down and his rank had not yet risen to prominence.

sentences.zh: 訓奏用士良分守澄之權，乃以士良為左軍中尉；

translations.literal: Xun memorialized to employ Shiliang to divide Shoucheng's power, and Shiliang was made Left Army Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: Xun memorialized to employ Shiliang to divide Shoucheng's power, and Shiliang was appointed Left Army Commandant;

sentences.zh: 守澄不悅，兩相矛盾。

translations.literal: Shoucheng was displeased, and the two were mutually at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng was displeased, and the two men fell into open conflict.

sentences.zh: 訓因其惡。

translations.literal: Xun exploited his displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: Xun exploited his displeasure.

sentences.zh: ，帝令內養李好古齏鴆賜守澄，秘而不發，守澄死，仍贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the inner attendant Li Haogu to bring poisoned broth as a gift to Shoucheng; the matter was kept secret and not publicized. When Shoucheng died, he was still posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the inner attendant Li Haogu to bring Shoucheng poisoned broth as a gift. The matter was kept secret. When Shoucheng died, the court still posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其弟守涓為徐州監軍，召還，至中牟，誅之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shoujuan served as army supervisor of Xuzhou; he was recalled, and when he reached Zhongmou he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shoujuan was army supervisor of Xuzhou. He was recalled, and when he reached Zhongmou he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 守澄豢養訓、註，反罹其禍，人皆快其受佞，而惡訓、註之陰狡。

translations.literal: Shoucheng reared and nurtured Xun and Zhu, yet in the end suffered their disaster; everyone rejoiced at his suffering for favoring flatterers, and hated the secret craft of Xun and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng had nurtured Xun and Zhu, yet in the end he fell victim to them. Men rejoiced at his fate for favoring flatterers, and condemned the secret craftiness of Xun and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 李訓既殺守澄，復惡鄭註，乃奏用註為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: Li Xun, having caused Shoucheng's death, again hated Zheng Zhu and therefore memorialized to appoint Zhu military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xun had brought about Shoucheng's death, he turned against Zheng Zhu and memorialized to appoint Zhu military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 訓欲盡誅宦官，乃與金吾將軍韓約、新除太原節度使王璠、新除邠寧節度使郭行餘、權御史中丞李孝本、權京兆尹羅立言謀。

translations.literal: Xun wished to execute all the eunuchs and therefore conspired with General of the Gold Crow Han Yue, the newly appointed military commissioner of Taiyuan Wang Fan, the newly appointed military commissioner of Binning Guo Xingyu, the acting Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Xiaoben, and the acting metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao Luo Liyan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun plotted to slaughter every eunuch. He conspired with General of the Gold Crow Han Yue, the newly appointed military commissioner of Taiyuan, Wang Fan, the newly appointed military commissioner of Binning, Guo Xingyu, the acting Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Xiaoben, and the acting metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, Luo Liyan.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月二十一日，上御宣政殿，百僚班定，韓約不奏平安，乃奏曰：「臣當仗廨內石榴樹，夜來降甘露，請陛下幸仗舍觀之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month of that year, the emperor presided at Xuanzheng Hall; when the hundred officials had taken their places, Han Yue did not report peace and security but memorialized, saying: "Within my barracks office there is a pomegranate tree; last night sweet dew descended upon it. I beg Your Majesty to proceed to the barracks quarters to view it.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month of that year, the emperor held court at Xuanzheng Hall. When the hundred officials had taken their places, Han Yue did not deliver the customary report of peace and security. Instead he said, "Within my barracks office there is a pomegranate tree. Last night sweet dew descended upon it. I beg Your Majesty to come to the barracks quarters and see it for yourself.

sentences.zh: 」帝乘輦趨金吾仗。

translations.literal: " The emperor mounted his carriage and hurried to the Gold Crow barracks.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor mounted his carriage and hurried to the Gold Crow barracks.

sentences.zh: 中尉仇士良與諸官先往石榴樹觀之，伺知其詐；

translations.literal: Commandant Qiu Shiliang and the various officials went first to view the pomegranate tree and secretly knew it was a deception;
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Qiu Shiliang and the other officials went ahead to inspect the pomegranate tree and secretly perceived the fraud;

sentences.zh: 又聞幕下兵仗聲，蒼黃而還，奏曰：「南衙有變。

translations.literal: then heard the sound of weapons beneath the curtain wall, and in panic returned, memorializing: "There is trouble in the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing weapons beneath the curtain wall, they fled back in alarm and reported, "There is an uprising in the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 」遂扶帝輦入閣門。

translations.literal: " They then supported the emperor's carriage into the Gate Tower.
translations.idiomatic: " They then escorted the emperor's carriage through the Gate Tower.

sentences.zh: 李訓從輦大呼曰：「邠寧、太原之兵，何不赴難？

translations.literal: Li Xun followed the carriage and shouted loudly: "The armies of Binning and Taiyuan—why do you not rush to the rescue?
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun followed the carriage and cried out, "The armies of Binning and Taiyuan—why do you not come to the rescue?

sentences.zh: 衛乘輿者，人賞百千！

translations.literal: Whoever guards the imperial carriage—a reward of a hundred or a thousand per man!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever guards the imperial carriage will receive a reward of a hundred or a thousand per man!

sentences.zh: 」於是誰何之卒，及御史臺從人，持兵入宣政殿院，宦官死者甚眾。

translations.literal: " Thereupon patrol guards and attendants of the Censorate, weapons in hand, entered the Xuanzheng Hall courtyard; very many eunuchs were killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon patrol guards and attendants from the Censorate, weapons in hand, stormed into the courtyard of Xuanzheng Hall, and a great many eunuchs were killed.

sentences.zh: 輦既入閣門，內官呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Once the carriage had entered the Gate Tower, the inner officials shouted "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: Once the carriage had passed through the Gate Tower, the inner officials shouted, "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 俄而士良等率禁兵五百餘人，露刃出東上閣逢人即殺，王涯、賈餗、舒元輿、李訓等四人宰相及王璠、郭行餘等十一人，屍橫闕下。

translations.literal: Before long Shiliang and others led more than five hundred forbidden troops, bared blades, out through the Upper Eastern Gate Tower, killing whomever they met. The four chancellors Wang Ya, Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu, and Li Xun, together with Wang Fan, Guo Xingyu, and eleven others in all—their corpses lay strewn beneath the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shiliang and others led more than five hundred palace troops with bared blades out through the Upper Eastern Gate Tower, killing anyone they met. The four chancellors Wang Ya, Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu, and Li Xun, together with Wang Fan, Guo Xingyu, and eleven others in all lay dead beneath the gate tower.

sentences.zh: 自是權歸士良與魚弘志。

translations.literal: From this time power passed to Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: From this time forward power passed to Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 至宣宗即位，復誅其太甚者，而閽寺之勢，仍握軍權之重焉。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne he again executed the most excessive among them, yet the power of the gate officials still held the weight of military authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne he executed the worst offenders among them, yet eunuch power still held the weight of military authority.

sentences.zh: =田令孜=

translations.literal: = Tian Lingzi =
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi

sentences.zh: 田令孜，本姓陳。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi's original surname was Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi was originally surnamed Chen.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，從義父入內侍省為宦者。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong era he entered the Palace Domestic Service as a eunuch with his adoptive father.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era he entered the Palace Domestic Service as a eunuch alongside his adoptive father.

sentences.zh: 頗知書，有謀略，自諸司小使監諸鎮用兵，累遷神策中尉、左監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was quite literate and had strategy, rising from a petty attendant of various offices supervising military campaigns of the various garrisons until he was promoted repeatedly to Shence Commandant and Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was literate and shrewd, rising from a petty attendant who supervised military affairs at the various garrisons until he was promoted repeatedly to Shence Commandant and Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，盜起關東。

translations.literal: During the Qianfu era bandits rose in the east of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu era rebellion broke out east of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 諸軍誅盜，以令孜為觀軍容、制置左右神策、護駕十軍等使。

translations.literal: As the various armies suppressed the bandits, Lingzi was made Army Supervisor, Commissioner for Establishing the Left and Right Shence, and Commissioner of the Ten Armies Protecting the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies moved to suppress the rebels, Lingzi was appointed Army Supervisor, Commissioner for Establishing the Left and Right Shence Armies, and Commissioner of the Ten Armies Protecting the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 京師不守，從僖宗幸蜀。

translations.literal: When the capital could not be held, he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, he accompanied Emperor Xizong into exile in Shu.

sentences.zh: 鸞輿返正，令孜頗有匡佐之功，時令孜威權振天下。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the rightful course, Lingzi had considerable merit in aiding and supporting the throne; at that time Lingzi's awesome authority shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned to the capital, Lingzi had done much to restore the throne. At that time his power shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 時關中寇亂初平，國用虛竭，諸軍不給。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chaos in Guanzhong had just been pacified, state revenues were exhausted, and the various armies went unpaid.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the turmoil in Guanzhong had only just subsided, state revenues were empty, and the armies went unpaid.

sentences.zh: 令孜請以安邑、解縣兩池榷鹽課利，全隸神策軍。

translations.literal: Lingzi requested that the salt monopoly profits of the two pools at Anyi and Jie County entirely be assigned to the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi requested that the salt-monopoly profits from the pools at Anyi and Jie County be assigned entirely to the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 詔下，河中王重榮抗章論列，言使名久例隸當道，省賦自有常規。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Wang Chongrong of Hezhong submitted a forceful memorial in argument, stating that the salt commissioners had long by precedent belonged to the local circuit, and provincial levies had their own standing regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Wang Chongrong of Hezhong submitted a forceful memorial arguing that the salt commissioners had long belonged to the local circuit by precedent, and that provincial levies followed established regulations.

sentences.zh: 令孜怒，用王處存為河中節度使，重榮不奉詔。

translations.literal: Lingzi grew angry and installed Wang Chucun as military commissioner of Hezhong; Chongrong did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi grew angry and installed Wang Chucun as military commissioner of Hezhong, but Chongrong refused to obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 令孜率禁兵討之。

translations.literal: Lingzi led the forbidden army to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi led the palace armies against him.

sentences.zh: 重榮引太原軍為援，戰於沙苑，禁軍大敗。

translations.literal: Chongrong brought the Taiyuan army as reinforcements; they fought at Shayuan and the forbidden army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong called in the Taiyuan army as reinforcements. They fought at Shayuan, and the palace armies were routed.

sentences.zh: 京師復亂，僖宗出幸寶雞，又移幸山南，方鎮皆憾令孜生事。

translations.literal: The capital was again in turmoil; Xizong fled to Baoji, then moved his court to Shannan; the frontier garrisons all resented Lingzi for stirring up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The capital fell into chaos again. Xizong fled to Baoji, then moved his court to Shannan. The regional garrisons all blamed Lingzi for stirring up trouble.

sentences.zh: 令孜懼，引前樞密楊復恭代己，從幸梁州，求為西川監軍。

translations.literal: Lingzi feared; he brought in the former secretariat chief Yang Fugong to replace himself, followed the emperor to Liang Prefecture, and requested appointment as army supervisor of West River.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for himself, Lingzi brought in the former secretariat chief Yang Fugong to replace him, followed the emperor to Liang Prefecture, and asked to be made army supervisor of West River.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使陳敬瑄，即令孜之弟也。

translations.literal: The military commissioner of West River, Chen Jingxuan, was Lingzi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner of West River, Chen Jingxuan, was Lingzi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 昭宗即位，三川大亂。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong ascended the throne, the Three River regions were in great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong ascended the throne, the Three River regions were in chaos.

sentences.zh: 詔宰相韋昭度鎮西川，陳敬瑄不受代。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the chief minister Wei Zhaodu to take command of West River; Chen Jingxuan refused to be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chief Minister Wei Zhaodu to take command of West River, but Chen Jingxuan refused to step down.

sentences.zh: 令孜引閬州刺史王建為援，建素以父事令孜。

translations.literal: Lingzi brought in the prefect of Lang Prefecture, Wang Jian, as reinforcements; Jian had long treated Lingzi as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi brought in Wang Jian, the prefect of Lang Prefecture, as reinforcement. Jian had long regarded Lingzi as a father figure.

sentences.zh: 時建方亂東川，聞其召也，以西蜀可圖，欣然赴之。

translations.literal: At that time Jian was just then stirring trouble in East River; when he heard the summons, judging that West Shu could be seized, he gladly went to answer it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jian was campaigning in East River. When he heard the summons, he judged West Shu ripe for the taking and gladly answered it.

sentences.zh: 建以所領千餘兵至漢州，陳敬瑄以建雄豪難制，辭而遣之。

translations.literal: Jian arrived at Han Prefecture with more than a thousand troops under his command; Chen Jingxuan, considering Jian bold and difficult to control, made excuses and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Jian marched to Han Prefecture with more than a thousand troops. Chen Jingxuan, finding him too bold and difficult to control, made excuses and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 建曰：「十軍阿父召予，及門而拒，鄰籓聞之，孰肯相容？

translations.literal: Jian said: "My adoptive father of the Ten Armies summoned me, and at his gate I am turned away—when neighboring garrisons hear of this, who will tolerate me?
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "The adoptive father of the Ten Armies summoned me, and now I am turned away at his gate. When neighboring circuits hear of this, who will suffer me to remain?

sentences.zh: 為予報令公，建至此，無所歸也。

translations.literal: Report on my behalf to the Commandant: having come this far, Jian has nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Tell the Commandant for me: Jian has come this far and has nowhere else to go.

sentences.zh: 」遂遣使上表，請討陳敬瑄以自效。

translations.literal: " He then dispatched envoys to submit a memorial requesting to campaign against Chen Jingxuan in proof of his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent envoys with a memorial offering to campaign against Chen Jingxuan to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，即命昭度為招討，入蜀加兵，經年無功，昭度還京。

translations.literal: The court praised this and immediately appointed Zhaodu as punitive commissioner; entering Shu he increased his troops, but after a year without success Zhaodu returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the plan and immediately appointed Zhaodu punitive commissioner. He entered Shu with reinforcements, but after a year without success Zhaodu returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 建遂絕棧道，不通詔使。

translations.literal: Jian then cut the plank roads and blocked imperial envoys bearing edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then severed the plank roads and blocked imperial envoys bearing edicts.

sentences.zh: 歲中急擊成都，陳敬瑄計窘，遣令孜出城，與建通和。

translations.literal: Within the year he pressed the attack on Chengdu; Chen Jingxuan, at his wits' end, sent Lingzi out of the city to negotiate peace with Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he pressed hard against Chengdu. Chen Jingxuan, at his wits' end, sent Lingzi out of the city to parley with Jian.

sentences.zh: 建竟自為蜀帥，令孜以義父之故，依倚仍舊監軍事。

translations.literal: Jian ultimately made himself military commander of Shu; because of the relation as adoptive father, Lingzi continued to rely on him and still supervised army affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jian ultimately made himself military commander of Shu. Because of their adoptive-father bond, Lingzi continued to rely on him and still supervised army affairs.

sentences.zh: 既而陳敬瑄遇鴆，令孜亦為建所殺。

translations.literal: Before long Chen Jingxuan met with poison; Lingzi was also killed by Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chen Jingxuan was poisoned, and Jian killed Lingzi as well.

sentences.zh: =楊復光=

translations.literal: = Yang Fuguang =
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fuguang

sentences.zh: 楊復光，內常侍楊玄價之養子也。

translations.literal: Yang Fuguang was the adopted son of the Palace Attendant Yang Xuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fuguang was the adopted son of Palace Attendant Yang Xuanjia.

sentences.zh: 幼以宦者入內侍省，慷慨負節義，有籌略，為小黃門，監鎮兵征討。

translations.literal: From youth he entered the Palace Domestic Service as a eunuch; he was magnanimous and possessed of principled loyalty, had strategy, served as a junior palace attendant, and supervised garrison troops on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he entered the Palace Domestic Service as a eunuch. Magnanimous and possessed of principled loyalty, he was also shrewd. As a junior palace attendant he supervised garrison troops on campaign.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，賊渠黃巢之犯江西，復光為排陣使，遣判官吳彥弘入城喻朝旨，巢即令其將尚君長奉表歸國。

translations.literal: During the Qianfu era, when the bandit chieftain Huang Chao invaded Jiangxi, Fuguang served as battle formation commissioner and dispatched his staff officer Wu Yanhong into the city to explain the court's intent; Chao then ordered his general Shang Junzhang to submit a memorial returning to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu era, when the bandit chieftain Huang Chao invaded Jiangxi, Fuguang served as battle formation commissioner and sent his aide Wu Yanhong into the city to explain the court's intent. Chao then ordered his general Shang Junzhang to submit a memorial offering allegiance.

sentences.zh: 招討使宋威害其功，並兵擊賊，巢怒，復作剽。

translations.literal: The punitive commissioner Song Wei usurped his achievement, combined armies to attack the bandits; Chao grew angry and again turned to raiding.
translations.idiomatic: The punitive commissioner Song Wei stole credit for the achievement and combined forces to attack the rebels. Chao grew enraged and resumed raiding.

sentences.zh: 朝廷誅尚君長，怨怒愈深。

translations.literal: The court executed Shang Junzhang; resentment and anger grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: The court executed Shang Junzhang, and Chao's resentment grew ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 宋威戰敗，復光總其兵權，進攻洪州，擒賊將徐唐莒。

translations.literal: Song Wei was defeated in battle; Fuguang assumed overall military authority, advanced to attack Hong Prefecture, and captured the bandit general Xu Tangju.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei was defeated in battle. Fuguang assumed overall command, advanced to attack Hong Prefecture, and captured the rebel general Xu Tangju.

sentences.zh: 詔以荊南節度使王鐸為招討，代宋威。

translations.literal: An edict appointed the military commissioner of Jingnan, Wang Duo, as punitive commissioner to replace Song Wei.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Wang Duo, military commissioner of Jingnan, punitive commissioner in Song Wei's place.

sentences.zh: 復光監忠武軍，屯於鄧州，以遏賊沖。

translations.literal: Fuguang supervised the Zhongwu Army, encamped at Deng Prefecture, to block the bandits' thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang supervised the Zhongwu Army, encamped at Deng Prefecture to block the rebels' advance.

sentences.zh: 京師陷賊，節度使周岌受偽命，賊使往來旁午。

translations.literal: The capital fell to the bandits; the military commissioner Zhou Ji accepted the false appointment; rebel envoys came and went incessantly.
translations.idiomatic: The capital fell to the rebels. Military Commissioner Zhou Ji accepted a commission from the rebels, and rebel envoys came and went without pause.

sentences.zh: 岌嘗夜宴，急召復光。

translations.literal: Ji once held a night banquet and urgently summoned Fuguang.
translations.idiomatic: One night Ji held a banquet and urgently summoned Fuguang.
