sentences.zh: 左右曰：「周公歸賊，必謀害內侍，不如勿往。

translations.literal: His attendants said: "Lord Zhou has submitted to the bandits and will surely plot to harm the Palace Attendant—it would be better not to go.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "Lord Zhou has gone over to the rebels and will surely plot to harm you. It would be better not to go.

sentences.zh: 」復光曰：「事勢如此，義不圖全。

translations.literal: " Fuguang said: "Matters stand as they do; one bound by principle does not seek to save himself alone.
translations.idiomatic: " Fuguang said, "Matters stand as they do. A man bound by principle does not plot to save himself alone.

sentences.zh: 」即赴之。

translations.literal: " He immediately went to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately went.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，岌言本朝事，復光因泣下。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep, Ji spoke of affairs of the dynasty, and Fuguang wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone deep, Ji spoke of the dynasty, and Fuguang wept.

sentences.zh: 良久曰：「丈夫所感者恩義，而規利害，非丈夫也。

translations.literal: After a long while he said: "What a true man is moved by is gratitude and principle; to weigh profit and loss is not the act of a true man.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he said, "A true man is moved by gratitude and principle. To weigh profit and loss is not worthy of a true man.

sentences.zh: 公自匹夫享公侯之貴，豈舍十八葉天子而北面臣賊，何恩義利害之可言乎！

translations.literal: You rose from a common man to enjoy the nobility of a duke or marquis—how could you abandon the emperor of eighteen generations and bow north to serve bandits? What talk can there be of gratitude, principle, profit, or loss!
translations.idiomatic: You rose from common birth to the nobility of duke or marquis. How could you abandon the emperor of eighteen generations and bow north to serve rebels? What talk can there be of gratitude or treachery!

sentences.zh: 」聲淚俱發，岌亦為之流涕。

translations.literal: " His voice and tears burst forth together, and Ji also wept for it.
translations.idiomatic: " His voice broke and tears streamed forth, and Ji wept as well.

sentences.zh: 岌曰：「吾不能獨力拒賊，貌奉而心圖之，故召公。

translations.literal: Ji said: "I cannot resist the bandits alone by force; outwardly I submit while inwardly I plot against them—therefore I summoned you.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "I cannot resist the rebels alone. Outwardly I submit while inwardly I plot against them. That is why I summoned you.

sentences.zh: 」瀝酒為盟。

translations.literal: " They poured out wine to seal their alliance.
translations.idiomatic: " They poured out wine and swore their alliance.

sentences.zh: 是夜，復光遣其養子守亮殺賊使於傳舍。

translations.literal: That night Fuguang had his adopted son Shouliang kill the rebel envoy at the relay station.
translations.idiomatic: That night Fuguang had his adopted son Shouliang kill the rebel envoy at the relay station.

sentences.zh: 時秦宗權叛岌，據蔡州。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Zongquan rebelled against Ji and occupied Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin Zongquan rebelled against Ji and seized Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復光得忠武之師三千入蔡州，說宗權，俾同義舉。

translations.literal: Fuguang obtained three thousand troops of the Zhongwu Army and entered Cai Prefecture, persuading Zongquan to join in the loyal cause.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang obtained three thousand Zhongwu troops and entered Cai Prefecture, persuading Zongquan to join the loyal cause.

sentences.zh: 宗權遣將王淑率眾萬人從復光收荊襄。

translations.literal: Zongquan dispatched the general Wang Shu leading ten thousand men to follow Fuguang in recovering Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan sent the general Wang Shu with ten thousand men to follow Fuguang in recovering Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 次鄧州，王淑逗留不進，復光斬之，並其軍，分為八都。

translations.literal: When they reached Deng Prefecture, Wang Shu halted and would not advance; Fuguang executed him, absorbed his army, and divided it into eight commands.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Deng Prefecture, Wang Shu halted and refused to advance. Fuguang executed him, absorbed his army, and divided it into eight commands.

sentences.zh: 鹿晏弘、晉暉、李師泰、王建、韓建等，皆八都之大將也。

translations.literal: Lu Yanhong, Jin Hui, Li Shitai, Wang Jian, Han Jian, and others were all great generals of the eight commands.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanhong, Jin Hui, Li Shitai, Wang Jian, Han Jian, and others were all senior generals of the eight commands.

sentences.zh: 進攻南陽，賊將硃溫、何勤來逆戰。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Nanyang, the bandit generals Zhu Wen and He Qin came to oppose them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to attack Nanyang, they met the rebel generals Zhu Wen and He Qin in battle.

sentences.zh: 復光敗之，進收鄧州，獻捷行在，五月也。

translations.literal: Fuguang defeated them, advanced to recover Deng Prefecture, and presented the victory to the mobile court—it was the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang defeated them, recovered Deng Prefecture, and presented the victory to the mobile court in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 復光乘勝追賊，至藍橋，丁母憂還。

translations.literal: Fuguang pursued the bandits on the momentum of victory to Lanqiao, then withdrew to observe mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang pursued the rebels in victory as far as Lanqiao, then withdrew to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 尋起復，受詔充天下兵馬都監，押諸軍入定關輔。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled from mourning; he received an edict appointing him overall supervisor of armies and horses, leading the various armies to secure Guan and the auxiliary capital regions.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled from mourning and appointed overall supervisor of armies and horses, leading the combined armies to secure the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 王重榮為東面招討使，復光以兵會之。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong served as eastern punitive commissioner; Fuguang joined him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong served as eastern punitive commissioner, and Fuguang joined him with troops.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，至河中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year he reached Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year he reached Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 賊將硃溫守同州，復光遣使諭之。

translations.literal: The bandit general Zhu Wen defended Tong Prefecture; Fuguang dispatched envoys to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Zhu Wen held Tong Prefecture. Fuguang sent envoys to persuade him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 九月，溫以所部來降。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wen came to surrender with the troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhu Wen surrendered with the troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 時賊將李翔守華州，巢寇益盛，王重榮憂之。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit general Li Xiang held Hua Prefecture; Chao's raids grew ever more severe; Wang Chongrong was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebel general Li Xiang held Hua Prefecture, Huang Chao's raids grew ever fiercer, and Wang Chongrong was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 謂復光曰：「臣賊則負國，拒戰則兵微，今日成敗，未可知也，公其圖之。

translations.literal: He said to Fuguang: "If I submit to the bandits I betray the state; if I resist in battle my forces are few—today success or failure cannot be known. Sir, devise a plan for this.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Fuguang, "If I submit to the rebels I betray the state; if I resist, my forces are too few. Today success or failure hangs in the balance. Sir, you must devise a plan.

sentences.zh: 」復光曰：「雁門李僕射以雄武振北陲，其家尊與吾先世同患難。

translations.literal: " Fuguang said: "Vice Censor-in-Chief Li of Yanmen, with his martial prowess, shook the northern frontier; his honored father and my forebears shared the same hardships.
translations.idiomatic: " Fuguang said, "Vice Censor-in-Chief Li of Yanmen shook the northern frontier with his martial prowess. His honored father and my forebears shared the same hardships.

sentences.zh: 李雁門奮不顧身，自播遷已來，征兵未至者，蓋太原阻路也。

translations.literal: Li of Yanmen would exert himself without regard for his own person; since the court's displacement, the reason troops summoned have not arrived is presumably because Taiyuan blocks the road.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Yanmen would throw himself into battle without regard for his own life. Since the court went into exile, the reason summoned troops have not arrived is that Taiyuan lies blocking the road.

sentences.zh: 如以朝旨諭鄭公，詔到，其軍必至。

translations.literal: If we use the court's mandate to inform the Duke of Zheng, when the edict arrives his army will surely come.
translations.idiomatic: If we use the court's mandate to inform the Duke of Zheng, when the edict arrives his army will surely come.

sentences.zh: 」重榮曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Chongrong said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " Chongrong said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」王鐸遣使奉墨詔之太原，太原以兵從之。

translations.literal: " Wang Duo dispatched envoys bearing the ink edict to Taiyuan; Taiyuan came with troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Duo dispatched envoys bearing the handwritten edict to Taiyuan, and Taiyuan sent troops in response.

sentences.zh: 及收京城，三敗巢賊，復光與其子守亮、守宗等身先犯難，功烈居多。

translations.literal: When the capital was recovered, having thrice defeated Chao's bandits, Fuguang and his sons Shouliang, Shouzong, and others personally took the lead in braving danger; their achievements and exploits were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was recovered, having thrice defeated Huang Chao's rebels, Fuguang and his sons Shouliang, Shouzong, and others personally led the charge. Their achievements were foremost among all.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，卒於河中，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year he died at Hezhong; he was forty-two years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year he died at Hezhong, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 復光雖黃門近幸，然慷慨有大志，善撫士卒；

translations.literal: Although Fuguang was a favored attendant of the Yellow Gate, he was nevertheless magnanimous and had great ambition, and was skilled at comforting troops;
translations.idiomatic: Although Fuguang was a favored palace attendant, he was magnanimous and ambitious, and skilled at winning the loyalty of his troops;

sentences.zh: 及死之日，軍中慟哭累日。

translations.literal: On the day of his death the army mourned and wept for many days.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his death the army mourned and wept for days on end.

sentences.zh: 身後平賊立功者，多是復光部下門人故將也。

translations.literal: Among those who later pacified bandits and won distinction, many were Fuguang's former disciples and veteran officers.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who later pacified rebels and won distinction, many were Fuguang's former disciples and veteran officers.

sentences.zh: 諸假子：守亮，興元節度使；

translations.literal: Among the adopted sons: Shouliang, military commissioner of Xingyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Among his adopted sons: Shouliang, military commissioner of Xingyuan;

sentences.zh: 守宗，忠武節度使：守信，商州防禦使；

translations.literal: Shouzong, military commissioner of Zhongwu; Shouxin, defense commissioner of Shang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Shouzong, military commissioner of Zhongwu; Shouxin, defense commissioner of Shang Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 守忠，洋州節度使；

translations.literal: Shouzhong, military commissioner of Yang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong, military commissioner of Yang Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 其餘以守為名者數十人，皆為牧守將帥。

translations.literal: The rest, several dozen men named with Shou, were all prefects, governors, and generals.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen other adopted sons whose names contained Shou all served as prefects, governors, and generals.

sentences.zh: =楊復恭=

translations.literal: = Yang Fugong =
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong

sentences.zh: 楊復恭，貞元末中尉楊志廉之後。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong was a descendant of Commandant Yang Zhilian of the late Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong was a descendant of Commandant Yang Zhilian of the late Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 志廉子欽義，大中朝為神策中尉。

translations.literal: Zhilian's son Qinyi served as Shence Commandant during the Dazhong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilian's son Qinyi served as Shence Commandant during the Dazhong reign.

sentences.zh: 欽義子三人：玄翼、玄價、玄寔。

translations.literal: Qinyi had three sons: Xuanyi, Xuanjia, and Xuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Qinyi had three sons: Xuanyi, Xuanjia, and Xuanshi.

sentences.zh: 玄翼，咸通中掌樞密；

translations.literal: Xuanyi, during the Xiantong era, held charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyi, during the Xiantong reign, held charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 玄寔乾符中為右軍中尉；

translations.literal: During the Qianfu era Xuanshi served as Right Shence Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu reign Xuanshi served as Right Shence Commandant;

sentences.zh: 玄價，河陽監軍。

translations.literal: Xuanjia was army supervisor at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjia served as army supervisor at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 復恭，即玄翼子也。

translations.literal: Fugong was Xuanyi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong was Xuanyi's son.

sentences.zh: 以父，幼為宦者，入內侍省。

translations.literal: Because of his father, he became a eunuch while still young and entered the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his father he was made a eunuch while still a boy and entered the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 知書，有學術，每監諸鎮兵。

translations.literal: He was literate and learned, and regularly supervised the troops of the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was literate and well schooled, and regularly supervised troops in the various circuits.

sentences.zh: 龐勛之亂，監陣有功，自河陽監軍入為宣徽使。

translations.literal: During Pang Xun's rebellion he distinguished himself supervising the battle line and was transferred from Heyang army supervisor to Commissioner of the Directorate of Imperial Entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: During Pang Xun's rebellion he won merit supervising the battle line and was transferred from Heyang army supervisor to Commissioner of the Directorate of Imperial Entertainment.

sentences.zh: ，玄翼卒，起復為樞密使。

translations.literal: When Xuanyi died, [Fugong] was recalled from mourning and appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanyi died, Fugong was recalled from mourning and appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時黃巢犯闕，左軍中尉田令孜為天下觀軍容制置使，專制中外。

translations.literal: At that time Huang Chao assaulted the capital; Left Shence Commandant Tian Lingzi served as Commissioner for Army Supervision and Disposition Throughout the Realm and held dictatorial sway over court and provinces alike.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huang Chao assaulted the capital; Left Shence Commandant Tian Lingzi served as Commissioner for Army Supervision and Disposition Throughout the Realm and wielded dictatorial power over court and provinces alike.

sentences.zh: 復恭每事力爭得失，令孜怒，左授復恭飛龍使，乃稱疾退於藍田。

translations.literal: On every matter Fugong strove to contest the rights and wrongs; Tian Lingzi grew angry, demoted Fugong to Commissioner of the Flying Dragon Office, and Fugong then pleaded illness and retired to Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: On every matter Fugong fought hard over what was right and wrong; enraged, Tian Lingzi demoted him to Commissioner of the Flying Dragon Office, whereupon Fugong pleaded illness and withdrew to Lantian.

sentences.zh: 僖宗自蜀還京，田令孜出師失律，車駕再幸山南，復用復恭為樞密使，尋代令孜為右軍中尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu to the capital, Tian Lingzi suffered defeat in the field and the imperial carriage again took refuge in Shannan; Fugong was again made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and soon replaced Tian as Right Shence Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu to the capital, Tian Lingzi lost the field and the imperial carriage again took refuge in Shannan; Fugong was again made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and soon replaced Tian as Right Shence Commandant.

sentences.zh: 時行在制置，內外經略，皆出於復恭。

translations.literal: At that time all dispositions at the mobile court and all internal and external strategy issued from Fugong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time every disposition at the mobile court and every plan within and without issued from Fugong.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，授觀軍容使，封魏國公。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital he was appointed Commissioner of Army Supervision and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital he was appointed Commissioner of Army Supervision and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 僖宗晏駕，迎壽王踐祚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong died, [Fugong] welcomed Prince Shou to mount the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong died, Fugong welcomed Prince Shou to the throne.

sentences.zh: ，加開府、金吾上將軍，專典禁兵，既軍權在手，頗擅朝政。

translations.literal: [He was] further granted an office with separate establishment and made Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Guards, given exclusive charge of the palace armies; once military authority was in his hands he usurped control of court affairs to a considerable degree.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted an office with separate establishment and made Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Guards, with exclusive charge of the palace armies; once military power was in his hands he came to dominate court affairs to a considerable degree.

sentences.zh: 昭宗惡之，政事多訪於宰臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong disliked this; on state affairs he consulted mostly with his chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong resented this and consulted chief ministers on most affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 故韋昭度、張浚、杜讓能每有陳奏，即舉大中故事，稍抑宦者之權。

translations.literal: Accordingly whenever Wei Zhaodu, Zhang Jun, and Du Rangneng submitted memorials they cited precedents from the Dazhong reign to check eunuch power little by little.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly whenever Wei Zhaodu, Zhang Jun, and Du Rangneng submitted memorials they cited Dazhong-era precedents to curb eunuch power little by little.

sentences.zh: 上性明察，由是偏聽之釁生焉。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature discerning and perspicacious; from this the seeds of partial listening sprang up.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was by nature sharp-eyed and discerning, and from this the seeds of biased listening took root.

sentences.zh: 國舅王瑰，頗居中任事，復恭惡之，奏授黔南節度。

translations.literal: The emperor's maternal uncle Wang Gui held considerable sway at court; Fugong hated him and memorialized to have him appointed military commissioner of Qiannan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's maternal uncle Wang Gui held considerable sway at court; Fugong hated him and memorialized to have him appointed military commissioner of Qiannan.

sentences.zh: 至吉柏江，覆舟而沒，物議歸咎於復恭，上每切齒道復恭。

translations.literal: At Jibo River his boat capsized and he drowned; public opinion blamed Fugong, and the emperor ground his teeth whenever he spoke of Fugong.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jibo River his boat capsized and he drowned; public opinion blamed Fugong, and the emperor ground his teeth whenever Fugong's name was mentioned.

sentences.zh: 復恭假子天威軍使守立，權勇冠於六軍，人皆避之。

translations.literal: Fugong's adopted son Shouli, commander of the Tianwei Army, was in authority and courage foremost among the Six Armies, and everyone avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong's adopted son Shouli, commander of the Tianwei Army, was in authority and courage foremost among the Six Armies, and everyone gave him a wide berth.

sentences.zh: 上欲罪復恭，懼守立為亂，乃謂復恭曰：「吾要卿家守立在左右，可進來。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to punish Fugong but feared Shouli might raise a rebellion; he therefore told Fugong, "I want your household's Shouli at my side—you may send him in."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to punish Fugong but feared Shouli might rebel; he therefore told Fugong, "I want your household's Shouli at my side—send him in."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜姓李，名順節，恩寵特異，勢侔樞要。

translations.literal: [The emperor] then bestowed the surname Li and the name Shunjie; favor and grace were extraordinary, and his power rivaled that of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then bestowed the surname Li and the name Shunjie; favor and grace were extraordinary, and his power rivaled the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乃與復恭爭權，每中傷其陰事，授順節鎮海軍節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: [Shunjie] then contended with Fugong for power, repeatedly exposing his private affairs to harm him, and was appointed military commissioner of Zhenhai Army and acting chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shunjie then contended with Fugong for power, repeatedly exposing his private affairs to harm him, and was appointed military commissioner of Zhenhai Army and acting chief minister.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔復恭致仕，賜杖履。

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict ordered Fugong to retire and granted him a staff and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict ordered Fugong to retire and granted him a staff and shoes.

sentences.zh: 復恭既失勢，欲退止商山別居，第在昭化裏，近玉山營。

translations.literal: Having lost his power, Fugong wished to withdraw and live separately on Mount Shang; his mansion was in Zhaohua Ward, near Yushan Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost his power, Fugong wished to withdraw and live in seclusion on Mount Shang; his mansion stood in Zhaohua Ward, near Yushan Camp.

sentences.zh: 假子守信為玉山軍使，守信時候復恭於其第，或誣告雲玉山軍使與復恭謀亂，詔李順節率禁軍攻之。

translations.literal: His adopted son Shouxin was commander of Yushan Army; Shouxin often attended on Fugong at his mansion when someone falsely reported that the Yushan commander and Fugong were plotting rebellion, and an edict ordered Li Shunjie to lead the palace armies against them.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Shouxin was commander of Yushan Army; Shouxin often attended on Fugong at his mansion when someone falsely reported that the Yushan commander and Fugong were plotting rebellion, and an edict ordered Li Shunjie to lead the palace armies against them.

sentences.zh: 昭宗御延喜樓。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong took his place on the Yanxi Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong took his place on the Yanxi Tower.

sentences.zh: 守信以兵拒之，順節屢敗。

translations.literal: Shouxin held them off with troops, and Shunjie suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin held them off with troops, and Shunjie suffered defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 際晚，守信、復恭挈其族出通化門，趨興元。

translations.literal: As evening drew on, Shouxin and Fugong led their clans out through Tonghua Gate and fled toward Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: As evening fell, Shouxin and Fugong led their clans out through Tonghua Gate and fled toward Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 守信令部將張綰殿其後，綰戰敗，被擒。

translations.literal: Shouxin ordered his subordinate Zhang Wan to bring up the rear; Wan was defeated and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin ordered his subordinate Zhang Wan to bring up the rear; Wan was defeated and captured.

sentences.zh: 復恭至興元，節度使楊守亮乃糾合諸守義兄弟舉兵，以討順節為名。

translations.literal: When Fugong reached Xingyuan, military commissioner Yang Shouliang rallied the various Shouyi brothers to raise troops in the name of punishing Shunjie.
translations.idiomatic: When Fugong reached Xingyuan, military commissioner Yang Shouliang rallied the various Shouyi brothers to raise troops under the banner of punishing Shunjie.

sentences.zh: 天子詔李茂貞、王行瑜討之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven ordered Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 明年，守亮兵敗，復恭與守亮挈其族，將奔太原，入商山。

translations.literal: The following year Shouliang's army was defeated; Fugong and Shouliang led their clans intending to flee to Taiyuan and entered the Shang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shouliang's army was defeated; Fugong and Shouliang led their clans intending to flee to Taiyuan and entered the Shang Mountains.

sentences.zh: 至乾元縣，為華州兵所獲，執送京師，皆梟首於市。

translations.literal: At Qianyuan County they were seized by Hua Prefecture troops and escorted to the capital; all were decapitated and displayed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: At Qianyuan County they were seized by Hua Prefecture troops and escorted to the capital; all were decapitated and displayed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞收興元，進復恭前後與守亮私書六十紙，內訴致仕之由云：「承天是隋家舊業，大侄但積粟訓兵，不要進奉。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen took Xingyuan and presented sixty sheets of private correspondence exchanged between Fugong and Shouliang, in which Fugong explained why he had retired, writing: "Chengtian is the Sui family's old domain; my eldest nephew need only store grain and train troops and need not send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen took Xingyuan and presented sixty sheets of private correspondence exchanged between Fugong and Shouliang, in which Fugong explained why he had retired, writing: "Chengtian is the Sui family's old domain; my eldest nephew need only store grain and train troops and need not send tribute.

sentences.zh: 吾於荊榛中援立壽王，有如此負心，門生天子，既得尊位，乃廢定策國老。

translations.literal: I plucked Prince Shou from brambles and thorns to set him on the throne—yet so faithless; a pupil-emperor, once he gained the exalted seat, discarded the elder statesman who fixed the succession."
translations.idiomatic: I plucked Prince Shou from brambles and thorns to set him on the throne—yet so faithless; a pupil-emperor, once he gained the exalted seat, cast aside the elder statesman who fixed the succession."

sentences.zh: 」其不遜如是。

translations.literal: Such was the insolence of his language.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the insolence of his language.

sentences.zh: 後復恭假子彥博奔太原，收復恭骸骨，葬於介休縣之抱腹山。

translations.literal: Later Fugong's adopted son Yanbo fled to Taiyuan, recovered Fugong's bones, and buried them on Baofu Mountain in Jiexiu County.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fugong's adopted son Yanbo fled to Taiyuan, recovered Fugong's remains, and buried them on Baofu Mountain in Jiexiu County.

sentences.zh: 復恭之後，宦者西門重遂為右軍中尉。

translations.literal: After Fugong, the eunuch Xi Men Chong followed as Right Shence Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After Fugong, the eunuch Xi Men Chong became Right Shence Commandant.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞初並山南，兵眾強盛，干預朝政，宰相杜讓能與重遂等謀誅之。

translations.literal: When Li Maozhen first annexed the Shannan region his forces were mighty and he meddled in court affairs; chief minister Du Rangneng plotted with Chong and others to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Maozhen first annexed the Shannan region his forces were mighty and he meddled in court affairs; chief minister Du Rangneng plotted with Chong and others to kill him.

sentences.zh: 師興，為茂貞所敗，重遂被誅，乃以內官駱全瓘、劉景宣為左右軍中尉。

translations.literal: When the army marched out it was defeated by Li Maozhen; Chong was put to death, and the inner officials Luo Quanguan and Liu Jingxuan were made Left and Right Shence Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched out it was defeated by Li Maozhen; Chong was executed, and the inner officials Luo Quanguan and Liu Jingxuan were made Left and Right Shence Commandants.

sentences.zh: 春，李茂貞、王行瑜以兵入朝，殺宰相韋昭度、李溪。

translations.literal: That spring Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu entered the capital at the head of troops and killed chief ministers Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu entered the capital at the head of troops and killed chief ministers Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使李克用率師渡河，討邠、岐二帥，軍於渭北。

translations.literal: Hedong military commissioner Li Keyong led his army across the river to campaign against the two commanders of Bin and Qi and encamped north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong military commissioner Li Keyong led his army across the river to campaign against the two commanders of Bin and Qi and encamped north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 駱全瓘與茂貞宿衛將閻圭，脅天子幸岐州，昭宗蒼黃幸莎城。

translations.literal: Luo Quanguan and Li Maozhen's imperial guard general Yan Gui coerced the Son of Heaven to go to Qi Prefecture; Emperor Zhaozong fled in panic to Shayu.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Quanguan and Li Maozhen's imperial guard general Yan Gui coerced the Son of Heaven to go to Qi Prefecture; Emperor Zhaozong fled in panic to Shayu.

sentences.zh: 茂貞以太原問罪，乃誅全瓘、閻圭以自解。

translations.literal: When Li Maozhen came under Taiyuan's charge of wrongdoing he executed Quanguan and Yan Gui to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan pressed charges against him Li Maozhen executed Quanguan and Yan Gui to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 昭宗幸華州，宦官稍微。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong went to Hua Prefecture, and the eunuchs' influence diminished slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong went to Hua Prefecture, and eunuch influence diminished slightly.

sentences.zh: 及光化還宮，內官景務修、宋道弼復專國政，宰相崔胤深惡之，中外不睦。

translations.literal: When he returned to the palace in the Guanghua era the inner officials Jing Wuxiu and Song Daobi again monopolized state affairs; chief minister Cui Yin hated them deeply and discord between court and palace grew.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the palace in the Guanghua era the inner officials Jing Wuxiu and Song Daobi again monopolized state affairs; chief minister Cui Yin hated them deeply and discord between court and palace grew.

sentences.zh: 宰相徐彥若、王搏有度量，見其陰險相傾，懼危時事，嘗奏曰：「人君當務大體，平心御物，無有偏私。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Xu Yanruo and Wang Bo were men of breadth and measure; seeing how the factions schemed treacherously against each other they feared for the times and once memorialized: "A ruler should attend to the larger whole, govern with an even heart, and show no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Xu Yanruo and Wang Bo were men of breadth and measure; seeing how the factions schemed treacherously against each other they feared for the times and once memorialized: "A ruler should attend to the larger whole, govern with an even heart, and show no partiality.

sentences.zh: 偏任偏聽，古人所患。

translations.literal: Partial appointments and biased listening are what the ancients dreaded.
translations.idiomatic: Partial appointments and biased listening are what the ancients dreaded.

sentences.zh: 今中官怙寵，道路目之，皆知此弊，然未能卒改。

translations.literal: Today the inner officials rely on favor—the road watches them and all know this abuse, yet it cannot suddenly be ended.
translations.idiomatic: Today the inner officials rely on favor—people on the road watch them and all know this abuse, yet it cannot suddenly be ended.

sentences.zh: 俟多難漸平，以道消息之。

translations.literal: Wait until the many troubles gradually subside, and then gently persuade them by the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the many troubles gradually subside, and then gently persuade them by the Way.

sentences.zh: 陛下勿泄聖謨，啟其奸詐。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not leak your sacred designs and thereby awaken their crafty deceit."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not leak your sacred designs and thereby awaken their crafty deceit."

sentences.zh: 」崔胤知搏所奏，頗銜之，他日見上，曰：「王搏奸邪，已為敕使外應，不可在相位。

translations.literal: Cui Yin learned what Wang Bo had memorialized and nursed resentment; another day when he saw the emperor he said, "Wang Bo is treacherous and wicked—he already responds in secret to the edict commissioners and cannot remain in the chief ministership."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin learned what Wang Bo had memorialized and nursed resentment; another day when he saw the emperor he said, "Wang Bo is treacherous and wicked—he already responds in secret to the edict commissioners and cannot remain chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」二年六月，貶搏官，賜死於藍田。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year Wang Bo was demoted and ordered to commit suicide at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year Wang Bo was demoted and ordered to commit suicide at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 道弼、務修亦賜死。

translations.literal: Daobi and Wuxiu were likewise ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Daobi and Wuxiu were likewise ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 以樞密使劉季述、王奉先為兩軍中尉，出徐彥若鎮南海。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners Liu Jishu and Wang Fengxian were made commandants of the two armies, and Xu Yanruo was sent out to govern Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners Liu Jishu and Wang Fengxian were made commandants of the two armies, and Xu Yanruo was sent out to govern Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 崔胤秉政而排擯宦官，季述等外結籓侯，以為黨援。

translations.literal: Cui Yin held the government and pushed eunuchs aside; Jishu and the rest allied outward with regional lords as factional support.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin held the government and pushed eunuchs aside; Jishu and the rest allied outward with regional lords as factional support.

sentences.zh: 十一月六日，季述矯詔以皇太子監國，遂廢昭宗。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the eleventh month Jishu forged an edict putting the crown prince in charge of the realm and then deposed Emperor Zhaozong.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the eleventh month Jishu forged an edict putting the crown prince in charge of the realm and then deposed Emperor Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 居東內，奪傳國寶授太子。

translations.literal: He occupied the eastern inner palace, seized the imperial seal of transmission, and conferred it on the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He occupied the eastern inner palace, seized the imperial seal of transmission, and conferred it on the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 昭宗以何皇后宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was placed with Empress He in the palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong was placed with Empress He in the palace quarters.

sentences.zh: 數人隨行，幽於東宮。

translations.literal: Only a few attendants went with him; he was confined in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few attendants went with him; he was confined in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 季述手持銀禋，於上前以禋畫地數上罪狀，云：「某時某事，你不從我言，其罪一也。

translations.literal: Jishu held a silver ceremonial staff before the emperor and, tracing on the ground with it, enumerated the emperor's offenses, saying, "At such-and-such a time, in such-and-such a matter, you did not heed my words—that is your first offense.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu held a silver ceremonial staff before the emperor and, tracing on the ground with it, enumerated the emperor's offenses, saying, "At such-and-such a time, in such-and-such a matter, you did not heed my words—that is your first offense.

sentences.zh: 」其悖逆如此。

translations.literal: Such was his audacity and treason."
translations.idiomatic: Such was his audacity and treason."

sentences.zh: 乃令李師虔以兵圍之。

translations.literal: He then ordered Li Shiqian to surround [the emperor] with troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Li Shiqian to surround the emperor with troops.

sentences.zh: 鎔錫錮其扃镕鐍。

translations.literal: They melted tin to seal the door bolts and locks.
translations.idiomatic: They melted tin to seal the door bolts and locks.

sentences.zh: 時方凝冽，嬪御無被，哭聲聞於外。

translations.literal: The weather was then bitterly cold; the palace women had no quilts, and their weeping could be heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was then bitterly cold; the palace women had no quilts, and their weeping could be heard outside.

sentences.zh: 穴墻通食者兩月。

translations.literal: For two months food was passed through a hole breached in the wall.
translations.idiomatic: For two months food was passed through a hole breached in the wall.

sentences.zh: 十二月晦，崔胤等謀反正，誅季述、奉先，復迎昭宗即位，改元。

translations.literal: On the last day of the twelfth month Cui Yin and the others plotted restoration, executed Jishu and Fengxian, and again escorted Emperor Zhaozong to the throne, changing the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the twelfth month Cui Yin and the others plotted restoration, executed Jishu and Fengxian, and again escorted Emperor Zhaozong to the throne, changing the reign title.

sentences.zh: 其歲十一月，硃全忠寇河中華州，陷之；

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month Zhu Quanzhong raided Hezhong and Hua Prefecture and took them;
translations.idiomatic: That year in the eleventh month Zhu Quanzhong raided Hezhong and Hua Prefecture and took them;

sentences.zh: 京師震恐。

translations.literal: The capital trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The capital trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 中尉韓全誨請上且幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: Commandant Han Quanhui asked the emperor to take temporary refuge at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Han Quanhui asked the emperor to take temporary refuge at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 全忠追逼乘輿，兵圍鳳翔者累年。

translations.literal: Quanzhong pressed hard upon the imperial carriage; for years his troops besieged Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong pressed hard upon the imperial carriage; for years his troops besieged Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，茂貞殺兩軍中尉韓全誨、張弘彥、樞密使袁易簡、周敬容等二十二人，皆斬首，以布囊貯之，令學士薛貽矩送於全忠求和。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Li Maozhen executed the two armies' commandants Han Quanhui and Zhang Hongyan, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong, and twenty-two others in all—all were beheaded, their heads stowed in cloth sacks, and the academician Xue Yiju was ordered to deliver them to Quanzhong to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Li Maozhen executed the two armies' commandants Han Quanhui and Zhang Hongyan, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong, and twenty-two others in all—all were beheaded, their heads stowed in cloth sacks, and the academician Xue Yiju was ordered to deliver them to Quanzhong to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 是月，全忠迎駕還長安，詔以崔胤為宰相，兼判六軍諸衛。

translations.literal: That same month Quanzhong escorted the imperial carriage back to Chang'an; an edict made Cui Yin chief minister and additionally put him in charge of the Six Armies and guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Quanzhong escorted the imperial carriage back to Chang'an; an edict made Cui Yin chief minister and additionally put him in charge of the Six Armies and guard offices.

sentences.zh: 胤奏曰：「高祖、太宗承平時，無內官典軍旅。

translations.literal: Yin memorialized: "Emperors Gaozu and Taizong, in tranquil times, had no inner officials in command of armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yin memorialized: "Emperors Gaozu and Taizong, in tranquil times, had no inner officials in command of armies.

sentences.zh: 自天寶以後，宦官浸盛。

translations.literal: From the Tianbao era onward eunuchs grew steadily more powerful.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianbao era onward eunuchs grew steadily more powerful.

sentences.zh: 貞元、元和，分羽林衛為左、右神策軍，使衛從，令宦官主之，唯以二千人為定制。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan and Yuanhe eras the Yulin Guard was divided into Left and Right Shence Armies for imperial escort, placed under eunuch command with a fixed establishment of only two thousand men each.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan and Yuanhe eras the Yulin Guard was divided into Left and Right Shence Armies for imperial escort, placed under eunuch command with a fixed establishment of only two thousand men each.

sentences.zh: 自是參掌樞密。

translations.literal: From that point they shared management of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From that point they shared management of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 由是內務百司，皆歸宦者，上下彌縫，共為不法：大則傾覆朝政，小則構扇籓方。

translations.literal: Thereafter a hundred offices of inner administration fell to eunuchs; above and below patched over one another and together practiced unlawfulness—great affairs overturning court governance, small ones inciting frontier circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter a hundred offices of inner administration fell to eunuchs; above and below patched over one another and together practiced unlawfulness—great affairs overturning court governance, small ones inciting frontier circuits.

sentences.zh: 車駕頻致播遷，朝廷漸加微弱，原其禍作，始自中人。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was repeatedly driven to flight; the court grew ever weaker; tracing the origin of the disaster, it began with the inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage was repeatedly driven to flight; the court grew ever weaker; tracing the origin of the disaster, it began with the inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 自先帝臨御已來，陛下纂承之後，朋儕日熾，交亂朝綱，此不翦其本根，終為國之蟊賊。

translations.literal: From when the late emperor first held the throne down to Your Majesty's succession their clique grew daily fiercer and tangled the court statutes—unless this root is cut it will forever be the state's locust plague.
translations.idiomatic: From when the late emperor first held the throne down to Your Majesty's succession their clique grew daily fiercer and tangled the court statutes—unless this root is cut it will forever be the state's locust plague.

sentences.zh: 內諸司使務宦官主者，望一切罷之，諸道監軍使，並追赴闕廷，即國家萬世之便也。

translations.literal: All inner office posts held by eunuchs should be abolished at once, and military supervisors in every circuit summoned back to the capital court—that would be the state's blessing for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: All inner office posts held by eunuchs should be abolished at once, and military supervisors in every circuit summoned back to the capital court—that would be the state's blessing for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：

translations.literal: The edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The edict said:

sentences.zh: 宦官之興，肇於秦、漢。

translations.literal: The rise of eunuchs began in the Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of eunuchs began in the Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 趙高、閻樂，竟滅嬴宗；

translations.literal: Zhao Gao and Yan Le in the end extinguished the Ying house;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao and Yan Le in the end extinguished the Ying house;

sentences.zh: 張讓、段珪，遂傾劉祚。

translations.literal: Zhang Rang and Duan Gui likewise overturned the Liu throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang and Duan Gui likewise overturned the Liu throne.

sentences.zh: 肆其志則國必受禍，悟其事則運可延長。

translations.literal: When they indulged their ambitions the state inevitably suffered harm; when rulers perceived the matter the dynasty could be prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: When they indulged their ambitions the state inevitably suffered harm; when rulers perceived the matter the dynasty could be prolonged.

sentences.zh: 朕所以斷在不疑，祈天永命者也。

translations.literal: It is for this that I resolve without hesitation, praying Heaven for enduring mandate.
translations.idiomatic: It is for this that I resolve without hesitation, praying Heaven for enduring mandate.

sentences.zh: 先皇帝嗣位之始，年在幼沖，群豎相推，奄專大政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the late emperor's accession he was still in tender years; the eunuch clique pushed one another forward and suddenly monopolized great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the late emperor's accession he was still in tender years; the eunuch clique pushed one another forward and suddenly monopolized great affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是毒流宇內，兵起山東，遷幸三川，幾淪神器。

translations.literal: Poison then flowed through the realm; armies rose in Shandong; the court moved to the Three Rivers and nearly lost the divine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Poison then flowed through the realm; armies rose in Shandong; the court moved to the Three Rivers and nearly lost the throne.

sentences.zh: 回鑾之始，率土思安，而田令孜妒能忌功，遷搖近鎮，陳倉播越，患難相仍。

translations.literal: At the first return of the imperial carriage all the land longed for peace, yet Tian Lingzi envied talent and begrudged achievement, unsettled nearby circuits, chaos at Chencang and flight upon flight—hardship followed hardship.
translations.idiomatic: At the first return of the imperial carriage all the land longed for peace, yet Tian Lingzi envied talent and begrudged achievement, unsettled nearby circuits, chaos at Chencang and flight upon flight—hardship followed hardship.

sentences.zh: 洎朕纂承，益相侮慢，復恭、重遂逞其禍，道弼、季述繼其兇；

translations.literal: When I succeeded to the throne they grew ever more insulting and contemptuous; Fugong and Chong let loose their calamities, Daobi and Jishu succeeded their wickedness;
translations.idiomatic: When I succeeded to the throne they grew ever more insulting and contemptuous; Fugong and Chong let loose their calamities, Daobi and Jishu succeeded their wickedness;

sentences.zh: 幽辱朕躬，淩脅孺子。

translations.literal: They shamed and imprisoned my person and threatened the young heir.
translations.idiomatic: They shamed and imprisoned my person and threatened the young heir.

sentences.zh: 天復返正，罪己求安，兩軍內樞，一切假借。

translations.literal: When Tianfu restored order I confessed fault seeking peace, yet both armies and the inner secretariat were entirely entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianfu restored order I confessed fault seeking peace, yet both armies and the inner secretariat were entirely entrusted to them.

sentences.zh: 韓全誨等每懷憤惋，曾務報仇；

translations.literal: Han Quanhui and the others always nursed indignation and strove for revenge;
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanhui and the others always nursed indignation and strove for revenge;

sentences.zh: 視將相若血仇，輕君上如木偶。

translations.literal: They treated chief ministers and generals like mortal enemies and held the ruler lightly as a wooden puppet.
translations.idiomatic: They treated chief ministers and generals like mortal enemies and held the ruler lightly as a wooden puppet.

sentences.zh: 未周星歲，竟致播遷；

translations.literal: Before a single year had turned they again drove [the court] to flight;
translations.idiomatic: Before a single year had turned they again drove the court to flight;

sentences.zh: 及在岐陽，過於羈紲。

translations.literal: And at Qiyang the restraint exceeded mere bonds.
translations.idiomatic: And at Qiyang the restraint exceeded mere bonds.

sentences.zh: 上憂宗社傾墜，下痛民庶流離，茫然孤居，無所控告。

translations.literal: Above I grieved lest the altars of state collapse; below I ached at the people's exile and dispersion—alone in confusion with nowhere to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Above I grieved lest the altars of state collapse; below I ached at the people's exile and dispersion—alone in confusion with nowhere to appeal.

sentences.zh: 全忠位兼二柄，深識朕心，駐兵近及於三年，獨斷方誅於元惡。

translations.literal: Quanzhong holds both handles of power, deeply understands Our mind; his troops have been stationed nearby for nearly three years, and by his sole decision the arch-criminal has at last been executed.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong wields both civil and military authority, knows Our mind well, has kept his army near the capital for nearly three years, and by his own resolve has at last destroyed the chief culprit.

sentences.zh: 今謝罪郊廟，即宅宮闈，正刑當在於事初，除惡宜絕其根本。

translations.literal: Now having confessed guilt at the suburban altars and temples, he takes up residence in the inner palace; proper punishment should come at the beginning of the affair, and rooting out evil should sever its root.
translations.idiomatic: Having now offered thanks at the suburban altars and taken up residence in the inner palace, punishment should fall while the matter is fresh, and evil must be cut off at the root.

sentences.zh: 先朝及朕，五致播遷，王畿之氓，減耗大半；

translations.literal: The former court and We have five times been driven into exile; the people of the royal domain have been diminished by more than half;
translations.idiomatic: Under the previous reign and Our own the court has been driven into exile five times, and the population of the capital region has been reduced by more than half;

sentences.zh: 父不能庇子，夫不能室妻。

translations.literal: fathers could not shelter sons, husbands could not house wives.
translations.idiomatic: fathers could not protect their sons, husbands could not keep their wives at home.

sentences.zh: 言念於茲，痛深骨髓，其誰之罪？

translations.literal: Speaking and thinking of this, the pain reaches deep into the marrow—whose crime is it?
translations.idiomatic: To speak of it is to feel pain to the marrow—whose fault is this?

sentences.zh: 爾輩之由！

translations.literal: It is because of you lot!
translations.idiomatic: Yours alone!

sentences.zh: 帝王之為治也，內有宰輔卿士，外有籓翰大臣，豈可令刑餘之人，參預大政？

translations.literal: When emperors and kings govern, within there are chancellors, aides, and ministers; without there are frontier pillars and great ministers—how can those mutilated by punishment be allowed to participate in great affairs of state?
translations.idiomatic: In governing, emperors rely on chancellors and ministers within and on frontier commanders without—how could those who bear the mark of castration be allowed to meddle in great affairs of state?

sentences.zh: 況此輩皆朕之家臣也，比於人臣之家，則奴隸之流。

translations.literal: Moreover these people are all Our household servants; compared with the households of human ministers, they are of the class of slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover these men are Our household servants—in any minister's household they would rank as mere slaves.

sentences.zh: 恣橫如此，罪惡貫盈，天命誅之，罪豈能舍？

translations.literal: To run riot thus, their crimes filling the measure—Heaven's mandate condemns them; how can their guilt be spared?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they ran riot to this degree until their crimes overflowed; Heaven itself condemns them—how could their guilt be spared?

sentences.zh: 橫屍伏法，固不足矜，含容久之，亦所多愧。

translations.literal: To lie slaughtered under the law is hardly worth pity; to have borne with them so long is what shames Us most.
translations.idiomatic: That they should lie dead under the law is hardly cause for pity; that We tolerated them so long is what shames Us most.

sentences.zh: 其第五可範已下，並宜賜死。

translations.literal: From the Fifth Rank Ke Fan downward, all should be granted death.
translations.idiomatic: From Ke Fan of the fifth rank downward, all are to be granted death.

sentences.zh: 其在畿甸同華、河中，並盡底處置訖。

translations.literal: Those in the capital region, Tonghua, and Hezhong are all to be disposed of to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the capital region, in Tonghua, and in Hezhong are all to be dealt with to the last man.

sentences.zh: 諸道監軍使已下，及管內經過並居停內使，敕到並仰隨處誅夷訖聞奏。

translations.literal: Army supervisors of the various circuits and below, and inner attendants who passed through or lodged within their jurisdictions—when the edict arrives all are to be executed wherever they are, and completion reported.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisors in every circuit and below, and any inner attendants who passed through or lodged in their jurisdictions, are to be executed on the spot when this edict arrives, and completion reported.

sentences.zh: 已令準國朝故事，量留三十人，各賜黃絹衫一領，以備宮內指使，仍不得輒有養男。

translations.literal: It has been ordered according to the dynastic precedent to retain thirty in measure; each is given one yellow silk jacket to serve for inner-palace errands, and they may not again rear boys.
translations.idiomatic: By dynastic precedent We have ordered that thirty be retained, each given a yellow silk jacket for palace errands, and none may again rear adopted sons.

sentences.zh: 其左右神策軍，並令停廢。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Shence armies are all ordered halted and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Shence armies are both to be abolished.

sentences.zh: 是日，諸司宦官百餘人，及隨駕鳳翔群小又二百餘人，一時斬首於內侍省，血流塗地。

translations.literal: That day, more than a hundred eunuchs of the various offices, and another two hundred-odd hangers-on who had followed the court to Fengxiang, were all beheaded at once in the Palace Domestic Service; blood flowed and smeared the ground.
translations.idiomatic: That day more than a hundred eunuchs from the various offices and another two hundred followers who had accompanied the court to Fengxiang were beheaded at once in the Palace Domestic Service, and blood pooled across the ground.

sentences.zh: 及宮人宋柔等十一人，兩街僧道與內官相善者二十餘人，並笞死於京兆府。

translations.literal: Also palace woman Song Rou and eleven others, and more than twenty monks and Daoists of the two wards who were on good terms with inner officials, were all beaten to death at the Jingzhao prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: The palace woman Song Rou and eleven others, and more than twenty monks and Daoists of the two wards who had been close to the eunuchs, were beaten to death at the office of the Jingzhao governor.

sentences.zh: 內諸司一切罷之，皆歸省寺。

translations.literal: All inner bureaus were abolished at once and returned to the ministries and directorates.
translations.idiomatic: All the inner bureaus were abolished at once and their functions returned to the regular ministries.

sentences.zh: 自是京城並無宦宮，天子每宣傳詔命，即令宮人出入。

translations.literal: From this the capital had no eunuchs at all; whenever the Son of Heaven proclaimed and transmitted edicts, he ordered palace women to go in and out.
translations.idiomatic: From that time there were no eunuchs in the capital; whenever the emperor issued an edict, palace women carried it.

sentences.zh: 崔胤雖復仇快志，國祚旋亦覆亡，悲夫！

translations.literal: Though Cui Yin satisfied his wish for revenge, the dynastic fortune soon perished as well—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Though Cui Yin had his revenge, the dynasty soon perished as well—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：崇墉大廈，壯其楹磶。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Lofty walls and great halls are strengthened by their pillars and foundation stones.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Lofty walls and great halls depend on strong pillars and foundation stones.

sentences.zh: 殿邦禦侮，亦俟明德。

translations.literal: To shore up the state and repel insult likewise awaits bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: To defend the realm and repel insult likewise depends on enlightened virtue.

sentences.zh: 宵人意褊，動不量力。

translations.literal: Men of the night are narrow-minded; in action they do not measure their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs are narrow-minded and act without gauging their strength.

sentences.zh: 投鼠敗器，良堪太息。

translations.literal: To strike a rat and ruin the vessel—truly worth a deep sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Striking the rat and breaking the vessel—truly a cause for deep regret.
